text: 元歴二年正月十日、九郎大夫判官義經院御所へ參て、大藏卿泰經朝臣を以て奏聞せられけるは、「平家は神明にも放たれ奉り、君にもすてられ參せて、帝都を出で波の上に漂ふ落人となれり。然るを此三箇年が間、責落さずして多くの國々を塞げらるゝ事口惜候へば、今度義經に於ては鬼界、高麗、天竺、震旦までも平家を責落ざらん限りは王城へ歸るべからず。」と憑し氣に申されければ、法皇大きに御感有て、「相構へて夜を日に繼いで、勝負を決すべし。」と仰下さる。判官宿所に歸て東國の軍兵どもに宣ひけるは、「義經鎌倉殿の御代官として院宣を承はて、平家を追討すべし。陸は駒の足の及ばむを限り、海は櫓櫂の屆がん程責行べし。少しもふた心あらむ人々は、とう／＼これより歸らるべし。」とぞ宣ける。

annotation.translation: On the tenth day of the first month of the second year of Genryaku, he went to the residence of the Emperor Go-Shirakawa and reported through Councilor of State Taira no Yasutsune, saying, "The Taira clan has been abandoned even by the gods and has been forsaken by the sovereign; they have left the capital and become outlaws drifting upon the waves. Yet, it is regrettable that in these three years, they have not been pressed down and have been able to occupy many provinces. Therefore, unless Yoshitsune presses down the Taira all the way to the Ghost Realm, Koryo, India, and China, he shall not return to the capital." He declared this with a determined heart, and the Retired Emperor, greatly moved, said, "Then, let us fight day and night until the outcome is decided." Upon returning to his residence, the Councilor announced to the troops of the Eastern Provinces, "Yoshitsune, having received the Imperial Decree as the Emperor's deputy, must pursue and destroy the Taira. On land, press forward as far as the horse's legs can reach; on the sea, press forward as far as the oars can extend. Anyone who has even the slightest hesitation should return home immediately." Thus he announced.

text: さる程に八島には、隙ゆく駒の足疾くして、正月も立ち二月にも成りぬ。春の草暮て、秋の風に驚き、秋の風やんで、春の草になれり。送り迎へて、既に三年に成にけり。「都には東國より荒手の軍兵、數萬騎著て責下る。」とも聞ゆ。「鎭西より、臼杵、戸次、松浦黨同心して、押渡る。」とも申あへり。彼れを聞き是れをきくにも、唯耳を驚し、肝魂を消より外の事ぞなき。女房達は女院、二位殿をはじめまゐらせて差つどひて、「又如何なる浮目をか見んずらん。如何なる憂事をか聞かんずらん。」と歎きあひ悲みあへり。新中納言知盛卿宣ひけるは、「東國北國の者共も隨分重恩を蒙たりしかども、恩を忘れ、契を變じて、頼朝、義仲等に隨ひき。まして西國とてもさこそはあらむずらめと思ひしかば、都にて、いかんにもならんと思ひし者を。我身一つの事ならねば、心弱うあくがれ出でて、今日はかゝるうき目を見る口惜さよ。」とぞ宣ひける。誠に理と覺て哀なり。

annotation.translation: So it came to pass that at Yashima, the feet of the horses that rushed by were swift, and January had passed and February had come. With the spring grass gone, startled by the autumn wind; with the autumn wind subsiding, returned to the spring grass. They were sent and received, and already three years had passed. "From the Eastern Provinces, a vast army of common soldiers, numbering tens of thousands of cavalry, has come down to attack," it was heard. "From the Western Provinces, the Usuki, Tsugai, and Matsuura clans, joined in a common cause, have crossed over to attack," it was said. To hear this and that, there was nothing but the startling of ears and the fading of souls. The ladies-in-waiting, beginning with the retired Empress and the Lady of the Second Rank, gathered together and sighed, saying, "What sort of ill omens will they see? What sort of sorrowful news will they hear?" They lamented and wept together. The newly appointed Chamberlain, Lord Tomomori, declared, "The people of the Eastern and Northern Provinces, too, have received ample great favors, yet they have forgotten those favors, broken their oaths, and followed Yoritomo and Yoshinaka. Therefore, I thought, even more so with the Western Provinces, surely it must be so, and I thought that in the Capital, whatever happened would not come to pass. But since it is not merely a matter of my own person, my heart weakly and eagerly went out, and now I see this wretched fate; what a bitter regret." Truly, it is reasonable and sorrowful.

text: 同二月三日九郎大夫判官義經、都を立て、攝津國渡邊より舟ぞろへして、八島へ既に寄んとす。參河守範頼も同日に都を立て、攝津國神崎より兵船を汰へて、山陽道へ趣かんとす。

annotation.translation: On the same day, the third day of the second month, Jūrō Taifu Hangan Yoshitsune left the capital, gathered boats at Watanabe in Settsu Province, and was already preparing to land at Yashima. Mimasaka no Kami Noriyori also left the capital on the same day, dispatched military ships from Kanzaki in Settsu Province, and was heading toward the San'yōdō.

text: 同十三日伊勢大神宮、石清水、賀茂、春日へ官幣使を立らる。「主上竝に三種の神器事故なう返入れさせ給へ。」と神祇官の官人、諸々の社司、本宮本社にて祈誓申すべき由仰下さる。

annotation.translation: On the thirteenth day of the same month, an imperial envoy was dispatched to the Grand Shrine of Ise, Izumo Shrine, Kamo Shrine, and Kasuga Shrine. "The Emperor and the Three Sacred Treasures, due to the circumstances, should be returned," so the Emperor instructed the officials of the Bureau of Divinities, along with the priests of all shrines, to pray and take an oath at the main shrines.

text:
同十六日渡邊、神崎、兩所にて此日ごろ汰ける船ども、纜既に解んとす。折節北風木を折て烈う吹ければ、大浪に船共散々に打損ぜられて、出すに及ばず。修理の爲に、其日は留る。渡邊には大名小名寄合ひて、「抑船軍の樣は未調練せず、如何あるべき。」と評定す。梶原申けるは、「今度の合戰には船に逆櫓を立候はばや。」判官、
「逆櫓とはなんぞ。」梶原、「馬は駈んと思へば、弓手へも馬手へも廻し易し。船は
きと推もどすが大事候、艫舳に櫓を立違へ、わい楫を入て、どなたへも安う推す樣に
し候ばや。」と申ければ、判官宣ひけるは、「軍と云者は一引も引じと思ふだにもあ
はひ惡ければ、引は常の習なり。本より逃まうけしてはなんのよかるべきぞ。先づ門出の惡さよ。逆櫓を立うとも返樣櫓を立うとも、殿原の舟には百丁千丁も立給へ。義經は本の櫓で候はん。」と宣へば、梶原申けるは、「好き大將軍と申は、駈べき所をかけ、引くべき所を引いて、身を全し敵を亡すを以て、よき大將軍とはする候。片趣なるをば、猪武者とて、好きにはせず。」と申せば、判官、「猪鹿は知らず、軍は唯平攻に攻て、勝たるぞ心ちはよき。」と宣へば、侍共梶原に恐れて高くは笑はねども、目引き鼻引きさゞめきあへり。判官と梶原と、已にどし軍あるべしとさざめきあへり。

annotation.translation: On the sixteenth day, at Watanabe and Kamizaki, the ships that had been prepared around this time were about to be unmoored. Just then, a northerly wind broke the trees and blew fiercely, battering the ships in large waves so severely that they could not be launched. For repairs, they remained that day. At Watanabe, the great and minor lords gathered and deliberated, saying, "In the first place, the ships for war are not yet trained; what should be done?" Kajiwara said, "In this battle, if we were to set up reverse oars on the ships..." The Lord Gengor, "What are reverse oars?" Kajiwara, "If one intends to charge horses, it is easy to turn them to the archers' side or the horsemen's side. With ships, however, pushing them back quickly is of utmost importance. If we set the oars opposite at the stern and bow, insert the paddles, and make it so that we can push back easily to any direction..." he said. The Lord Gengor replied, "War, they say, means not to retreat even a single step. Even if we meet with difficulty, retreating is the usual practice. What good would it be to flee from the start? First, the shame of setting out. Whether we set up reverse oars or ordinary oars, let the Lord's boats be equipped with a hundred or a thousand oars. Yoshitsune will use the ordinary oars." When he said this, Kajiwara replied, "To be called a great general, one must charge where one should charge, retreat where one should retreat, preserve one's own life, and destroy the enemy; thus, one becomes a great general. To be one-sidedly aggressive is to be called a wild warrior, and one is not liked." When he said this, the Lord Gengor said, "I know not of boars and deer, but in war, I only wish to attack with plain, straightforward force and win." The samurai, fearing Kajiwara, did not laugh aloud but whispered among themselves with pulled eyes and noses. The Lord Gengor and Kajiwara had already whispered that a great battle would surely take place.

text:
漸々日暮れ夜に入ければ、判官宣ひけるは、「船の修理して新しうなたるに、各一種一瓶して祝給へ殿原。」とて、營む樣で船に物具いれ兵粮米積、馬共立させて、
「疾々仕れ。」と宣ひければ、水主梶取申けるは、「此風は追手にて候へども、普通
に過たる風で候。沖はさぞ吹候らん。爭か仕候べき。」と申せば、判官大に怒て宣ひ
けるは、「野山の末にてし、海河のそこにおぼれてうするも皆これせんぜの宿業也。
海上にいで浮うだる時風強きとていかゞする。向ひ風に渡らんと言ばこそ、僻事なら
め。順風なるが、少し過たればとて、是程の御大事に、爭か渡らじとは申ぞ。船仕ら
ずば一々にしやつ原射殺せ。」と下知せらる。奧州の佐藤三郎兵衞嗣信、伊勢三郎義
盛、片手矢はげ進み出で、「何條子細を申ぞ。御定であるに、とく／＼つかまつれ。
舟仕つらずば一々に射殺さんずるぞ。」といひければ、水主梶取是を聞て、「射殺れ
んも同事、風強くば、只馳死に死ねや者共。」とて、二百餘艘の舟の中に、唯五艘出
てぞ走りける。殘の船は風に恐るるか梶原に怖かして、皆留まりぬ。判官宣ひけるは、
「人の出ねばとて留まるべきにあらず、唯の時は敵も用心すらむ。かゝる大風大波に思も寄らぬ時におしよせてこそ思ふ敵を討ずれ。」とぞ宣ひける。五艘の船と申すは、先づ判官の船、田代の冠者、後藤兵衞父子、金子兄弟、淀江内忠俊とて、船奉行の乘たる船なり。判官宣ひけるは、「各の船に篝な燃そ。義經が船を本船として、艫舳の篝を守れや。火數多く見えば、敵も恐れて用心してんず。」とて終夜走る程に、三日に渡る所を、唯三時計に渡りけり。二月十六日の丑刻に、渡邊福島を出て、明る卯の時に、阿波の地へこそ吹著たれ。

annotation.translation: As the day gradually waned and night entered, the Gannan declared, "Repair the ships and make them new; each vessel shall receive one bottle as a celebratory gift, and proceed to the shipyard." With this, they prepared the ships, loading equipment and provisions, and mounted the horses, ordering, "Hurry and finish!" The boatmen and helmsmen replied, "Although this wind is at our backs, it is an ordinary wind; the open sea will surely blow fiercely. How can we possibly proceed?" Upon hearing this, the Gannan became greatly angry and declared, "Whether we perish at the end of wild mountains and forests or drown in the depths of the sea and rivers, this is all the karmic consequence we have earned. When we set out on the sea and float, even if the wind is strong, what will we do? If we say we will cross against the wind, it would surely be a strange thing. Since the wind is favorable, even if it is slightly strong, how can we not cross for such a great matter? If the ships are not prepared, I will shoot each one of you down." This order was issued. Sato Saburo Be-e Tsuginobu of Oshu, Ise Saburo Yoshimori, and Katateya Hage advanced bravely, saying, "What are you arguing about? This is the command; hurry and serve! If the boats are not prepared, I will shoot each one of you down." Upon hearing this, the boatmen and helmsmen replied, "Whether we are shot down, it is the same; if the wind is strong, let us all run and die." Among the more than two hundred ships, only five set out and sped away. The remaining ships, fearing the wind or terrified by Kajiwara, all stayed behind. The Gannan declared, "Just because no one has come forth, we should not stay; in ordinary times, the enemy might be on guard. But at such a time of great wind and great waves, when we attack unexpectedly, we can surely defeat the enemy we intended to strike." The five ships mentioned were, first, the Gannan's ship, the ships of Tashiro no Gon, Goto Be-e and his son, the Kaneko brothers, and Yodoe no Uchida Toshiyoshi, which were the ships of the ship administrator. The Gannan declared, "Light fires on each ship. Take Yoshitsune's ship as the main vessel, and guard the fires at the stern and bow. If many fires are seen, the enemy will surely be afraid and on guard." Thus, they ran throughout the night, crossing a distance that usually takes three days in merely three watch hours. Departing from Watanabe no Fukushima at the hour of the Ox on the sixteenth day of the second month, they arrived in Awaji at the bright hour of the Rabbit.

text:
夜既に明ければ、なぎさに赤旗少々閃いたり。判官、是を見て、「あはや我等が祝設けはしたりけるは。舟平付につけ、踏傾けて馬下さんとせば、敵の的に成て射られなんず。なぎさにつかぬ先に馬ども追下／＼船に引つけ／＼游せよ。馬の足立、鞍爪ひたるほどに成ばひたひたと乘て、駈よ者共。」とぞ下知せられける。五艘の船に、物具入、兵粮米積んだりければ、馬唯五十餘疋ぞ立たりける。なぎさ近くなりしかば、
ひた／＼と打乘て、喚てかくれば、渚に百騎許有ける者共、暫もこらへず、二町計颯
と引てぞのきにける。判官汀に打立て、馬の息休めておはしけるが、伊勢三郎義盛を
めして、「あの勢の中に、然るべい者やある。一人召て參れ。尋ぬべき事あり。」と
宣へば、義盛畏て承り、唯一騎かたきの中へ馳入り何とかいひたりけん、年四十計な
る男の、黒皮威の鎧著たるを、甲を脱せ、弓の弦弛せて、具して參りたり。判官、「何者ぞ。」と宣へば、「當國の住人坂西の近藤六親家」と申す。「何家にてもあらばあれ、物具な脱せそ。やがて八島の案内者に具せんずるぞ。其男に目放つな。迯て行かば射殺せ、者共。」とぞ下知せられける。「爰をば何くといふぞ。」と問はれければ「かつ浦と申候。」判官笑て、「色代な。」と宣へば、「一定かつ浦候。下臈の申やすいに付て、かつらとは申候へども、文字には勝浦と書て候。」と申す。判官、「是聞給へ、殿原。軍しに向ふ義經が、勝浦に著く目出度さよ。此邊に、平家の後矢射つべい者はないか。」「阿波民部重能が弟、櫻間介能遠とて候。」「いざさらば蹴散して通らん。」とて、近藤六が勢百騎許が中より、三十騎許すぐり出いて我勢にぞ具せられける。能遠が城に押寄て見れば、三方は沼、一方は堀。堀の方より押寄て、閧をどと作る。城の中の兵共、矢先をそろへて指つめ引つめ散々に射る。源氏の兵是を事ともせず。甲の錣を傾けをめきさけんで責入りければ、櫻間介叶はじとや思ひけむ。家子郎等に防矢射させ、我身は究竟の馬を持たりければ、打乘て稀有にして落にけり。判官防矢射ける兵共二十餘人が頸切懸て軍神に祭り、悦の鬨を作り、「門出よし。」とぞ宣ひける。判官近藤六親家を召て、「八島には平家の勢如何程有ぞ。」「千騎にはよも過候はじ。」「など少いぞ。」「かくのごとく四國の浦々島々に五十騎百騎づつ指置れて候。其上阿波民部重能が嫡子、田内左衞門教能は、河野四郎が、召せども參ぬを責めんとて、三千餘騎で伊豫へ越えて候。」「さてはよい隙ごさんなれ。是より八島へはいか程の道ぞ。」「二日路で候。」「さらば敵の聞ぬ先に寄よや。」とてかけ足に成つゝ、歩せつ、馳つ、引へつ、阿波と讃岐との境なる大坂越といふ山を終夜こそ越られけれ。

annotation.translation: When the night was already bright, a few red flags flashed on the shore. The Gon (Lord) saw this and said, 'Ah, it seems our festive preparations have been made. Let us fasten the boats, overturn them, and become targets for the enemy to shoot at. Before we reach the shore, let the horses be driven down and pulled into the boats. When the horses' feet are planted and their stirrups are taut, let us ride down swiftly and gallop, you all.' So he gave the order. On the five boats, with equipment loaded and rice provisions stacked, only about fifty horses were standing. Since the shore drew near, they rode down in a rush, shouting and laughing, and the hundred or so men who were at the shore could not hold out for even a moment; they fled two cho (approximately 200 meters) in a flash. The Gon stood on the shore, resting the horses' breath, and addressed Ise no Saburo Yoshimori: 'Among that force, is there anyone worthy? Summon one person here. There is something I must inquire of him.' Yoshimori, fearing, replied, 'Very well.' He rode into the midst of a single rider and said something. A man, about forty years of age, wearing a black lacquered armor with the horse's armor removed and the bowstring loosened, came forward fully equipped. The Gon asked, 'Who are you?' He replied, 'I am Kondo Rokushin'ye of Sakai, a resident of this province.' The Gon said, 'It does not matter what house you belong to; do not remove your armor. Soon I will have you serve as a guide for the Eight Islands. Do not let your eyes stray from that man. If he flees, kill him, you all.' So he gave the order. 'What is this place called?' he was asked. 'It is called Katsuura,' he replied. The Gon laughed and said, 'How appropriate.' 'Indeed, it is Katsuura. Since a lowly man like me finds it easy to say, although it is written in characters as Katsuura, it is pronounced Katsuura.' The Gon said, 'Listen to me, Lord Taira. It is fortunate that Yoshitsune, heading for war, has arrived at Katsuura. Is there anyone here who can shoot arrows at the rear of the Taira clan?' 'It is Sakurama no Sukenuen, the younger brother of Awa no Minbu Shigenori.' 'Then let us charge through and pass.' Thus, from among the hundred or so men of Kondo Rok's force, about thirty riders broke through and joined our side. When they pressed against Sakurama's castle, they found that on three sides there were marshes, and on one side a moat. Pressing from the direction of the moat, they raised a great clamor. The soldiers inside the castle, aligning their arrows, drew and shot them in a wild frenzy. The Minamoto soldiers did not consider this a matter of concern. Tipping their helmet crests, they shouted and charged in. Sakurama no Sukenuen must have thought, 'Shall I not resist?' He ordered his servants to shoot defensive arrows, but he himself, having a final reserve horse, rode down and, in a rare feat, fell into the water. The Gon had the twenty or more soldiers who were shooting defensive arrows killed and their heads cut off, honored them as war gods, raised a victory shout of joy, and declared, 'What a fine departure!' The Gon summoned Kondo Rokushin'ye and asked, 'How many Taira forces are there at the Eight Islands?' 'They are not less than a thousand.' 'Why so few?' 'Thus, in the bays and islands of Shikoku, fifty or a hundred riders are stationed at each. Moreover, Awa no Minbu Shigenori's legitimate son, Taino no Saemon Noshin, the son of Kono no Saburo, refuses to come even when summoned, so to punish him, he has crossed into Iyo with over three thousand riders.' 'Then there is a good opportunity. How far is the road to the Eight Islands from here?' 'It is two days' journey.' 'Then let us approach before the enemy hears of it.' With that, they began to run, walk, gallop, and pull, and crossed the night through the mountain called Oosaka-goe, which lies on the border between Awa and Sanuki.

text: 夜半許に、立文持たる男に行連て物語し給。此男夜の事ではあり、敵とは夢にも知らず。御方の兵共の八島へ參ると思ひけるやらん。打解て細々と物語をぞしける。「其文はいづくぞ。」「八島の大臣殿へ參り候。」「誰かまゐらせらるゝぞ。」「京より女房の參らせられ候。」「何事なるらん。」と宣へば、「別の事はよも候はじ。源氏既に淀河尻に出向うて候へば、それをこそ告げ申され候らめ。」「げにさぞ有らん。是も八島へ參るが、いまだ案内を知らぬに、じんじよせよ。」と宣へば、「是は度々參て候間、案内は存知して候。御供つかまつらん。」と申せば判官、「其文取れ。」とて、文ばいとらせ「しやつからめよ。罪作に頸なきそ。」とて、山中の木に縛附てぞ通られける。さて文を明て見給へば、げにも女房の文とおぼしくて、「九郎はすゝどき男士にて侍ふなれば、大風大波をも嫌はず寄せ侍らんと覺えさぶらふ。御勢ども散さで用心せさせ給へ。」とぞ書かれたる。判官、「是は義經に天の與へ給ふ文也。鎌倉殿に見せ申さん。」とて深う納て置れけり。

annotation.translation: At midnight, a man who carried a written letter came to the side of the bed and began to speak with him. This man knew nothing of the night's events, nor did he suspect any enemy. He must have thought that the soldiers of the Lord's side were going to Yashima. He loosened his guard and began to speak with him in a low voice. "Where is that letter?" "It is being delivered to the Minister of Yashima." "Who is delivering it?" "A lady is being sent from the capital." "What is the matter?" When he asked, "There is surely nothing else. Since the Minamoto clan has already set out for the end of the Yodo River, surely that is what they are telling you." "Indeed, that must be the case. This too is about going to Yashima, but since I do not yet know the way, show it to me." "Since I have been going there many times, I know the way. I shall accompany you." When he said this, the General said, "Bring that letter." He had the letter taken and, with the words, "I shall cut you down. There is no neck to be spared if you commit a crime," he had him tied to a tree in the mountains and passed by. Then, when he opened the letter and read it, he thought it was indeed a letter from a lady: "Since Gorō is a brave warrior, he will not shrink from great winds and great waves but will come. Let your forces not be scattered, but be careful." He wrote. The General said, "This is a letter from Heaven given to Yoshitsune. I shall show it to the Lord of Kamakura." He deeply accepted it and put it away.

text: 明る十八日の寅刻に、讃岐國ひけ田と云ふ所に打下りて、人馬の息をぞ休めける。其より丹生屋、白鳥、打過／＼、八島の城へ寄給ふ。又近藤六親家を召て、「八島の館の樣は、如何に。」と問ひ給へば、「知召されねばこそ候へ、無下に淺間に候。潮の干て候時は、陸と島との間は、馬の腹もつかり候はず。」と申せば、「さらばやがて寄よや。」とて、高松の在所に火を懸、八島の城へ寄せ給ふ。

annotation.translation: On the bright morning of the eighteenth day, at the hour of the tiger, they descended at a place called Hikeda in Sanuki Province to rest the men and horses. From there, they passed through Niouya and Shiratori, and came to the castle of Yashima. They summoned the six relatives of Kondo and asked, 'What is the situation at the mansion of Yashima?' He replied, 'Since you have not inquired, I shall not speak lightly. When the tide recedes, even the bellies of the horses cannot cross between the mainland and the island.' 'Then let us go immediately,' he said, and set fire to the place at Takamatsu, approaching the castle of Yashima.

text: 八島には、阿波民部重能が嫡子、田内左衞門教能、河野四郎が、召せども參らぬを責んとて、三千餘騎で伊豫へ越えたりけるが河野をば討漏して家子郎等百五十餘人が首きて、八島の内裏へ參せたり。「内裏にて賊首の實檢せられん事然るべからず。」とて、大臣殿の宿所にて實檢せらる。百五十六人が首也。頸ども實檢しける處に、者共、「高松の方に火出來たり。」とてひしめきあへり。「晝で候へば手過ではよも候はじ。敵の寄せて火を懸たると覺候。定めて大勢でぞ候らん。取籠られては叶ふまじ。とく／＼召され候へ。」とて、惣門の前のなぎさに船共つけならべたりければ、我も／＼と乘給ふ。御所の御船には、女院北政所二位殿以下の女房達召されけり。大臣殿父子は、一つ船に乘給ふ。其外の人々思ひ／＼に取乘て、或は一町許、或は七八段、五六段など漕出したる處に、源氏の兵共、直甲七八十騎、惣門の前のなぎさにつと出來たり。潮干がたの折節潮干る盛なれば、馬の烏頭、太腹に立つ所もあり。其より淺き所も有り。け上る潮の霞と共にしぐらうたる中より、白旗さと差上たれば、平家は運盡て、大勢とこそ見てんげれ。判官敵に小勢と見せじとて、五六騎七八騎十騎許、打群／＼出來たり。

annotation.translation: At Yashima, Awa no Minbu Shigenou, the legitimate son, Taida no Saemon Noshin, and Kono no Shiro were summoned, but when they did not come and were to be blamed, they crossed to Iyo with over three thousand riders, and after having Kono killed and having the heads of one hundred and fifty-plus housemen brought back, they came to the Imperial Palace at Yashima. "It is not proper to conduct a thorough inspection of the rebel leaders at the Imperial Palace," they said, so the inspection was carried out at the residence of the Minister. There were one hundred and fifty-six heads. While their necks were being thoroughly inspected, the men crowded together saying, "Fire has broken out in the Takamatsu direction." "Since it is daytime, it is unlikely to be an accident. We must have been attacked by the enemy who set the fire. Surely it is a large force. If we are surrounded, we cannot succeed. We must be summoned immediately," they said, and so boats were lined up on the shore before the main gate, and everyone boarded. In the Imperial Palace's boats, the ladies-in-waiting, including the Lady of the Northern House and the Second Rank, were summoned. The Minister and his son rode in one boat. The others boarded in various ways; some rowed out about a cho, others seven or eight ken, or five or six ken. At that moment, the soldiers of the Minamoto clan, some seventy or eighty riders in full armor, rushed out to the shore before the main gate. Since the tide was receding, there were places where the horses' heads were raised on their swollen bellies, and there were shallower places as well. As the receding tide's mist rose, a white flag was suddenly raised, and the Taira, having exhausted their fortune, were seen to be vastly outnumbered. The Deputy, not wishing to appear to the enemy as a small force, sent out five, six, seven, eight, or about ten riders, charging in groups.

text: 九郎大夫判官其日の裝束には、赤地の錦の直垂に、紫裾濃の鎧著て、金作の太刀を帶き、切斑の矢負ひ、滋籐の弓の眞中取て、船の方を睨へ、大音聲を上て、「一院の御使、檢非違使五位尉源義經」と名乘る。其次に伊豆國住人田代冠者信綱、武藏國住人金子十郎家忠、同與一親範、伊勢三郎義盛とぞ名乘たる。續いて名乘るは、後藤兵衞實基、子息新兵衞基清、奧州佐藤三郎兵衞嗣信、同四郎兵衞忠信、江田源三、熊井太郎、武藏坊辨慶と聲々に名乘てはせ來る。平家の方には、「あれ射取れや。」とて、或は遠矢に射る船も有り、或は差矢に射船も有り。源氏の兵共、弓手になしては射て通り、馬手になしては射て通り、上げ置いたる船の陰を、馬休め所にして、[1]をめき叫んて責戰ふ。

annotation.translation: On that day, Kyūrōdai no Kangō wore a kosode of brocade with a red ground and a dark purple hem, donned armor, carried a gold-mounted tachi, bore arrows with cut patterns, and held a Fuji bow in the middle of the grip, glared toward the boats, and loudly proclaimed, 'The envoy of the First Emperor, the Keniwaishi Gōi no Jo, Minamoto no Yoshitsune.' Next were named Tashiro no Kanja Nobutsuna, a resident of Izu Province; Kaneko Jūrō Iesada, a resident of Musashi Province; Tomo Yoichi Kinemasa; and Ise Saburō Yomori. Following them came Gōtō Hēe Sanebase, his son Shin Hēe Motokiyo, Ōshū Satō Saburō Hēe Tsuganobu, his younger brother Shijirō Hēe Tadazane, Eita Genzō, Kumai Tarō, and Musashibō Benkei, each calling out their names. On the Taira side, someone said, 'Shoot them down!' Some boats were hit by long-range arrows, others by close-range arrows. The Minamoto warriors, whether on foot or mounted, shot their arrows and passed by; they used the shadow of the boats left above as a place to rest their horses, [1] shouting loudly and pressing the attack.

text: 後藤兵衞實基は、古兵にて有ければ、軍をばせず、先内裏に亂入、手々に火を放て、片時の煙と燒拂ふ。大臣殿、侍どもを召て、「抑源氏が勢如何程あるぞ。」「當時僅に七八十騎こそ候らめ。」と申。「あな心憂や。髮の筋を一筋づゝ分けて取るとも、此勢には足まじかりけるものを。中に取籠討ずして、あわてゝ船に乘て、内裏を燒せつる事こそ安からね。能登殿はおはせぬか、陸へ上て一軍し給へ。」と宣へば、「承て候ぬ。」とて、越中次郎兵衞盛次を相具して小船に取乘て燒拂ひたる惣門のなぎさに陣を取る。判官八十餘騎、矢比に寄て引へたり。越中次郎兵衞盛次舟の面に立出で大音聲を揚て申けるは、「名乘れつるとは聞つれども、海上遙に隔たて其假名實名分明ならず。今日の源氏の大將軍は誰人でおはしますぞ。」伊勢三郎義盛歩ませ出て申けるは、「事も愚かや、清和天皇十代の御末、鎌倉殿の御弟九郎大夫判官殿ぞかし。」盛次、「さる事あり。一年平治の合戰に、父討れて孤にて有しが、鞍馬の兒にて、後には金商人の所從になり、粮料背負て奧州へ落惑ひし小冠者が事か。」とぞ申したる。義盛、「舌のやはらかなる儘に、君の御事な申そ。さいふわ人どもは、砥浪山の軍に追落されて辛き命生て、北陸道にさまよひ、乞食して泣／＼京へ上りたりし者か。」とぞ申ける。盛次重て申けるは、「君の御恩に飽滿て、何んの不足にてか、乞食をばすべき。さ言ふわどのこそ、伊勢の鈴鹿山にて山だちして、妻子をも養ひ、我身も過けるとは聞しか。」といひければ、金子十郎家忠「無益の殿原の雜言かな。我も人も虚言いひつけて雜言せんには誰か劣るべき。去年の春、一谷にて、武藏相模の若殿原の手なみの程は見てん物を。」と申所に弟の與一傍に有けるが、言せも果ず、十二束二ぶせよひいてひやうと放つ。盛次が鎧の胸板に、裏掻く程にぞ立たりける。其後は互に詞戰はとまりにけり。

annotation.translation: Goto Hebei Sanemoto, being an old soldier, did not form his ranks, but rushed straight into the Inner Palace, set fire here and there, and burned it down in a moment. The Minister, calling his attendants, said, "How many men does the Minamoto clan have, I wonder?" "Only seventy or eighty horsemen at most," they replied. "Alas, what a sorrowful thing! Even if I were to pluck out my hair strand by strand, this force would not suffice. It is not fitting that we should be trapped and forced to fight without capturing them; in a panic, we boarded a boat and set the Inner Palace ablaze. Where is Lord Noto? Please come ashore and lead an army." When he said this, they replied, "We understand," and, taking Echigo no Jiro Hebei Morihiro with them, boarded a small boat and took up a position on the flat ground before the gate they had burned. The Danjo had over eighty horsemen, who drew their bows at a distance. Echigo no Jiro Hebei Morihiro stood up on the bow of his boat and raised his voice, saying, "I have heard you declare your names, but from afar on the sea, your given and real names are not clear. Who is the great general of the Minamoto clan today?" Ise no Saburo Yoshiaki stepped forward and replied, "What foolishness! He is the ninth son of the Lord of Kamakura, the Lord Danjo, the last descendant of Emperor Seiwa's tenth generation." Morihiro said, "So it is. In the Battle of Hie in the first year of the Hogen era, my father was killed, and I was left an orphan. I was a child of Kurama, and later became a servant of a gold merchant. I carried provisions and fled in confusion to the province of Oshu, little crown-prince. Is that the man?" Yoshiaki said, "With such a soft tongue, do not speak of your lord's affairs! Are you not one of those who were driven back from the battle of Tohiwa Mountain, barely keeping your lives, wandered the Hokuriku Road, begged, wept, and ascended to Kyoto?" Morihiro replied again, "Sated with your lord's grace, what lack is there that I should beg? It is said that the one who did this was the man who, at Suzuka Mountain in Ise, took up arms in the mountains, supported his wife and children, and even survived himself." Hearing this, Kinoko no Jiro Iekata said, "What useless and frivolous words from the Danjo! If anyone is to weave lies and speak nonsense, who could be inferior to me? Last spring, at Ichitani, I witnessed the manner of the young lords of Musashi and Sagami in the field." As he spoke, his brother Yoichi, standing nearby, did not finish his words but drew twelve bundles of arrows, twisted them, and loosed them. They struck the breastplate of Morihiro's armor, standing there as if scraping from the inside. After that, the verbal duel ceased.

text:
能登守教經「船軍はやうある物ぞ。」とて鎧直垂は著給はず、唐卷染の小袖に、唐綾威の鎧著て、いか物作の大太刀帶き、二十四差たるたかうすべうの矢負ひ、滋籐の弓を持給へり。王城一の強弓精兵にておはせしかば、矢先に廻る者、射透さずと云ふ事なし。中にも九郎大夫判官を射倒さむとねらはれけれども、源氏の方にも心得て、
奧州の佐藤三郎兵衞嗣信、同四郎兵衞忠信、伊勢三郎義盛、源八廣綱、江田源三、熊
井太郎、武藏坊辨慶など云ふ一人當千の兵共、吾も吾もと馬の首を立竝て大將軍の矢
面に塞りければ、力及び給はず。「矢面の雜人原そこのき給へ。」とて、差詰引詰
散々に射給へば、矢場に鎧武者十餘騎計射落さる。中にも眞先に進んだる奧州の佐藤
三郎兵衞が弓手の肩を馬手の脇へつと射拔れて、暫もたまらず、馬より、倒にどうと
落つ。能登殿の童に、菊王と云ふ大力の剛の者あり、萌黄威の腹卷に、三枚甲の緒をしめて、白柄の長刀の鞘を外し、三郎兵衞が首を取らんと、走りかゝる。佐藤四郎兵衞兄が頸を取せじと、よ引てひやうと射る。童が腹卷の引合せをあなたへつと射ぬかれて、犬居に倒れぬ。能登守是を見て、急て舟より飛んで下り、左の手に弓を持ながら、右の手で菊王丸を提て、船へからりと投られたれば、敵に頸は取られねども、痛手なれば死にけり。是は、本は越前の三位の童なりしが、三位討たれて後、弟の能登守に仕はれけり。生年十八歳にぞなりける。此童を討せて、餘に哀に思はれければ、其後は軍もし給はず。

annotation.translation: Noto-no-kami Takanori, wearing a straight armor (yoroi) over his under-robe, a small-sleeved garment of Tang-style dye, and a cuirass of Tang-style lacquered leather, equipped with a great sword of the 'Ika-mono' type, carrying twenty-four arrows of the 'Takau-sube' type, and holding a Shitō bow, was present. As he was the strongest archer and finest soldier in the Imperial Capital, there was no one who could avoid being pierced by his arrows. In particular, he was targeted to bring down the Nine-Lord Magistrate (Kuro-dai-kan), but the Minamoto side had anticipated this. Among them were Sato Saburo Be-e Tsugunobu of the Ou province, his younger brother Sato Shiro Be-e Tadatsugu, Ise Saburo Yoshi-mori, Genba Hironari, Eda Genzo, Kumai Taro, Musashi-bō Benkei, and others—each a soldier capable of facing a thousand men. They lined up their horses' heads, each shouting "Me! Me!" and blocked the path of the Great General's arrows, so his strength could not reach them. Then, shouting "You commoner in the midst of the arrow field, come here!", he shot them relentlessly, causing more than ten armored horsemen to fall to the ground. Among them, he shot out the shoulder of the archer of Sato Saburo Be-e, who had advanced at the very front, into the side of his horse's harness, and the man, unable to endure even a moment, fell headlong from his horse. Noto-no-dono had a young page named Kiku-no-Miko, a powerful and strong youth. He wore a cinnabar-colored lacquered breastplate, tied the cords of a three-layered cuirass, removed the scabbard of a long sword with a white handle, and rushed forward to take the head of Saburo Be-e. Sato Shiro Be-e, the elder brother of the younger Sato, shouted "Do not let him take my neck!" and shot with a forceful pull. The page's breastplate cords were shot through to the front, and he fell into the dog-fence (a type of enclosure). Seeing this, Noto-no-kami quickly leaped from his boat, holding his bow in his left hand, and, lifting Kiku-no-Maro in his right hand, threw him into the boat with a light motion. Although his neck was not taken by the enemy, the wound was severe, and he died. This youth was originally a page of the Mi-ri of Echizen Province, and after the Mi-ri was slain, he served under the younger brother, Noto-no-kami. He was eighteen years of age. After slaying this youth, others felt great sorrow, and thus he ceased to fight further.

text: 判官は佐藤三郎兵衞を陣の後へ舁入れさせ、馬より下り、手をとらへて、「三郎兵衞如何覺ゆる。」と宣へば、息の下に申けるは、「今はかうと存じ候。」「思置事はなきか。」と宣へば、「何事をか思置候べき。君の御世に渡らせ給はんを見參せで、死に候はん事こそ口惜う覺候へ。さ候はでは、弓箭取ものの、敵の矢にあたり死なん事、本より期する所で候也。就中に源平の御合戰に、奧州の佐藤三郎兵衞嗣信と云ける者、讃岐國八島の磯にて、主の御命に替り奉て討れけりと、末代の物語に申さん事こそ弓矢取る身は今生の面目、冥途の思出にて候へ。」と申もあへず、唯弱りに弱りにければ、判官涙をはら／＼と流し、「此邊に貴き僧やある。」とて、尋出し、「手負の唯今落入に、一日經書て弔へ。」とて、黒き馬の太う逞いに、金覆輪の鞍置て、彼僧に給にけり。判官五位尉になられし時、五位になして、大夫黒と呼れし馬也。一谷の鵯越をも此馬にてぞ落れたりける。弟の四郎兵衞を始として、是を見る兵共、皆涙をながし、「此君の御爲に命を失はん事、全く露塵程も、惜からず。」とぞ申ける。

annotation.translation: The Gon-no-Kami had Sato Saburo-be-e carried to the rear of the camp; he dismounted from his horse, took his hand, and said, "How do you feel, Saburo-be-e?" In a faint voice, he replied, "I am feeling thus now." "Do you have any lingering thoughts?" he asked again. "What thoughts could I possibly have?" he answered. "To die without seeing you, my lord, cross over to the next world would be most regrettable. If that were not the case, then for one who takes up bow and arrow, to be struck by the enemy's arrow and die is something I have expected from the beginning. Especially in the conflict between the Genji and Heike, there was a man named Sato Saburo-be-e Tsuginobu of the Oshu province, who at the shore of Hishima in Sanuki Province, offered his life in place of his master's and was struck down. In the tales of later generations, it is said that for one who takes up bow and arrow, one's present life is one's honor, and one's memories in the underworld are what matter." Before he could finish speaking, he grew weak and weaker. The Gon-no-Kami shed tears profusely and said, "Is there a noble monk nearby?" Upon inquiry, a monk was brought forth. "This wounded man is now about to fall into the earth; pray for him for one day," he said, and placed him on a black horse, sturdy and powerful, fitted with a saddle of gold-rimmed wheels, and gave it to that monk. This was the horse called "Taima-kuro" when the Gon-no-Kami was appointed to the rank of Go-i-no-jo; it was a horse of the rank of Go-i. It was even this horse upon which the bird-slope of Hitotani was descended. Seeing this, the soldiers, starting with his younger brother Shiro-be-e, all shed tears and said, "To lose our lives for this lord, not even to the extent of a dust mote, is not regrettable at all."

text: さる程に、阿波讃岐に平家を背て、源氏を待ける者共、あそこの嶺、こゝの洞より、十四五騎廿騎、うちつれ／＼參りければ、判官程なく三百餘騎にぞ成にける。「今日は日暮ぬ、勝負を決すべからず。」とて、引退く處に、沖の方より尋常に飾たる小船一艘、汀へ向ひて漕よせけり。磯へ七八段ばかりに成しかば、船を横樣になす。あれは如何にと見る程に、船の中より、年の齡十八九ばかりなる女房の誠に優に美しきが、柳の五衣に、紅の袴著て皆紅の扇の日出したるを、船のせがひに挾み立て、陸へ向てぞ招いたる。判官後藤兵衞實基を召て、「あれは如何に。」と宣へば、「射よとにこそ候めれ。但し大將軍の矢面に進んで、傾城を御覽ぜば手だれにねらうて、射落せとの計ごとと覺え候。左も候へ。扇をば射させらるべうや候らん。」と申。「射つべき仁は御方に誰かある。」と宣へば、「上手ども幾等も候中に、下野國の十人、那須太郎資高が子に與一宗高こそ、小兵で候へども、手ききて候へ。」「證據はいかに。」と宣へば、「かけ鳥などを爭うて、三に二は必射落す者で候。」「さらば召せ。」とて召されたり。與一其比は二十許の男士也。かちに赤地の錦を以て、おほくびはた袖色へたる直垂に、萌黄威の鎧著て、足白の太刀を帶き、切斑の矢の其日の軍に射て少々殘たりけるを首高に負ひ成し薄切斑に鷹の羽作交たるぬた目の鏑をぞ指副たる。滋籐の弓脇に挾み、甲をば脱ぎ高紐に懸け、判官の前に畏る。「如何に宗高、あの扇の眞中射て平家に見物せさせよかし。」與一畏て申けるは、「射おほせ候はん事不定に候。射損じ候なば、ながき御方の御瑕にて候べし。一定仕らんずる仁に仰附らるべうや候らん。」と申。判官大に怒て、「鎌倉を立て、西國へ趣かん殿原は、義經が命を背べからず。少も仔細を存ぜん人は、とう／＼是より歸るべし」とぞ宣ひける。與一重て辭せば惡かりなんとや思ひけん、「外づれんは知候はず、御諚で候へば仕てこそ見候はめ。」とて、御前を罷立、黒き馬の太う逞に、小房の鞦かけ、まろほや摺たる鞍置てぞ乘たりける。弓取直し、手綱かいくり、汀へ向いて歩ませければ、御方の兵共後を遙に見送て、「此若者一定仕り候ぬと覺候。」と申ければ、判官も憑し氣にぞ見給ひける。矢比少し遠かりければ、海へ一段ばかり打入たれども、猶扇の交ひ、七段ばかりは有るらんとこそ見えたりけれ。比は二月十八日の酉の刻ばかりの事なるに、折節北風烈くて、磯打浪も高かりけり。船はゆりあげゆり居ゑたゞよへば、扇も串に定らずひらめいたり。沖には平家船を一面に竝べて見物す。陸には源氏轡を竝べて、是を見る。何れも／＼晴ならずと云ふ事ぞなき。與一目を塞いで、「南無八幡大菩薩、別しては我國の神明、日光權現宇都宮、那須湯泉大明神、願は、あの扇の眞中射させて給せ給へ。是を射損ずる物ならば、弓伐折自害して、人に二度面を向ふべからず。今一度本國へむかへんと思召さば、此矢はづさせ給ふな。」と、心の中に祈念して、目を見開いたれば、風も少し吹弱り、扇もいよげにぞ成たりける。與一鏑を取て番ひ、よ引いてひやうと放つ。小兵と云ふぢやう十二束三伏、弓は強し、浦響く程長鳴して、あやまたず扇の要際一寸許置いて、ひふつとぞ射切たる。鏑は海へ入ければ、扇は空へぞ擧りける。暫は虚空に閃めきけるが、春風に一もみ二もみもまれて、海へさとぞ散たりける。夕日の輝いたるに皆紅の扇の日出したるが白波の上に漂ひ、浮ぬ沈ぬゆられければ、沖には平家ふなばたを扣て感じたり。陸には源氏箙を扣てどよめきけり。

annotation.translation: In this manner, the men who had turned their backs on the Taira in Awa and Sanuki, waiting for the Minamoto, from that ridge and from this cave, came riding forth in groups of fourteen, fifteen, twenty riders. Soon the number of the Dan'gō's followers swelled to over three hundred. 'The day is now waning; we cannot decide the battle today,' he said, and as he prepared to withdraw, a small boat, neatly adorned and rowed steadily from the open sea toward the shore, came into view. When it reached about seven or eight steps from the shore, the boat was turned sideways. As they wondered what it could be, a young lady, no more than eighteen or nineteen years of age, exceedingly beautiful and charming, emerged from the boat. She was dressed in a willow-green five-layered robe and a crimson skirt, and holding a red fan with a sunburst pattern, she stood on the gunwale of the boat and beckoned toward the land. The Dan'gō summoned Gōtōbē no Tane'ki and asked, 'What is that?' He replied, 'They seem to be urging us to shoot. However, it may be a plan by the Great General to test us by having us advance upon the face of the enemy and shoot down a beauty. Even so, might we not be allowed to shoot the fan?' The Dan'gō asked, 'Is there anyone among us capable of such a shot?' The reply was, 'Among our many skilled archers, the ten men from Shimotsuke Province, particularly Yūichi Mune'kane, the son of Jūtō Satake, though he is a small man, is highly skilled.' 'What is the evidence?' asked the Dan'gō. 'When competing to shoot at flying birds, he certainly hits two out of three,' came the answer. 'Then summon him,' the Dan'gō ordered, and he was called. Yūichi was then about twenty years old. He wore a crimson brocade garment over a wide-sleeved hitatare of pale green, with armor lacquered in green. A white-handled sword was at his waist, and on his head he carried a few arrows from the day's battle, which were still left over. These were arranged with a pattern of cut spots, and he wore a quiver with an eagle's feather design. He tucked a lacquered bow under his arm, removed his armor, and hung it from a high cord, then respectfully approached the Dan'gō. 'Mune'kane,' the Dan'gō said, 'shoot the very center of that fan so that the Taira may watch.' Yūichi, bowing respectfully, replied, 'It is uncertain whether I may be permitted to shoot. If I miss, it will be a great disgrace to you. Might I not be ordered by someone who is certain to succeed?' The Dan'gō, greatly angered, declared, 'Those who intend to establish Kamakura and advance to the Western Provinces must not turn their backs on Yoshitsune's command. Anyone who hesitates should return at once.' Hearing this, Yūichi thought, 'If I were to refuse, I would be deemed a traitor, for I am acting under your order.' He bowed, withdrew from the presence, and mounted a sturdy black horse equipped with a small saddle and a finely polished stirrup. He adjusted his bow and reins, turned toward the shore, and began to walk. The Dan'gō's soldiers watched him from afar and said, 'That young man will certainly succeed.' The Dan'gō, though somewhat impatient, looked on. Since the distance was a little far, he threw himself one step into the sea, yet the fan still appeared to be about seven steps away. This was around the hour of the Rooster on the eighteenth day of the second month. At that time, the north wind blew fiercely, and the waves crashing against the shore were high. The boat bobbed up and down, and the fan, not fixed to its stick, fluttered. In the open sea, the Taira ships were lined up to watch; on the land, the Minamoto soldiers stood with their quivers in hand, also watching. No one spoke of anything but that the wind was not favorable. Yūichi covered his eyes and prayed, 'Namu Hachiman Daibosatsu, especially the deities of our country, the Sun God, Utsunomiya, and the Numa Onsen Great Deity, I pray that you allow me to shoot the very center of that fan. If I miss, I will break my bow, commit suicide, and never again show my face to anyone. If you wish to return me to my homeland once more, do not let this arrow miss.' With this prayer in his heart, he opened his eyes. The wind subsided slightly, and the fan seemed to become more still. Yūichi took his arrow, nocked it, drew the bow, and released it with a sharp cry. Though he was a small man, his strength was great; the bow roared like the sea, and without missing, he cut the very center of the fan, leaving only about an inch of the shaft intact. The arrow tip fell into the sea, and the fan rose into the air. For a moment it shimmered in the void, but as the spring wind blew, it fluttered and scattered into the sea. The red fan, with its sunburst pattern, floated upon the white waves under the setting sun, rising and falling with the waves. In the open sea, the Taira clapped their hands in admiration; on the land, the Minamoto bowed their heads in silence.

text: 餘りの面白さに、感に堪ざるにやと覺しくて船の中より、年五十許なる男の、黒革威の鎧著て白柄の長刀持たるが、扇立たりける所に立てまひすましたり。伊勢三郎義盛、與一が後へ歩せ寄て、「御諚ぞ、仕れ。」と云ひければ、今度は中差取て打くはせ、よ引いてしや頸の骨をひやうふつと射て船底へまさかさまに射倒す。平家の方には音もせず、源氏の方には又箙を扣いて、どよめきけり。「あ射たり。」といふ人も有り、又「情なし。」と云ふ者もあり。平家是を本意なしとや思ひけん、楯ついて一人、弓持て一人、長刀持て一人、武者三人なぎさにあがり、楯を衝て「敵寄せよ。」とぞ招いたる。判官、「あれ、馬強ならん若黨共、馳寄せて蹴散せ。」と宣へば、武藏國の住人、三穗屋四郎、同藤七、同十郎、上野國の住人、丹生の四郎、信濃國の住人、木曾の中次、五騎つれて、をめいて駈く。楯の影より、塗箆に、黒ほろ作だる大の矢をもて、眞先に進だる三穗屋の十郎が馬の左の胸懸づくしを、ひやうづばと射て筈の隱る程ぞ、射籠だる。屏風を返す樣に、馬はどうと倒るれば、主は馬手の足をこえ弓手の方へ下立て、軈て太刀をぞ拔だりける。楯の陰より、大長刀打振て懸りければ、三穗屋の十郎、小太刀大長刀に叶はじとや思けむ、かいふいて迯ければ、軈て續て追懸たり。長刀でながんずるかと見る處に、さはなくして、長刀をば左の脇にかい挾み、右の手を差延て、三穗屋十郎が甲のしころをつかまむとす。つかまれじとはしる。三度つかみはづいて、四度の度むずとつかむ。暫したまて見えし。鉢附の板より、ふつと引切てぞ迯たりける。殘四騎は、馬を惜うでかけず、見物してこそ居たりけれ。三穗屋十郎は、御方の馬の陰に逃入て、息續居たり。敵は追ても來で長刀杖につき、甲のしころを指上げ、大音聲を上て、「日比は音にも聞つらん。今は目にも見給へ。是こそ京童部の喚なる上總惡七兵衞景清よ。」と名乘棄てぞ歸りける。

annotation.translation: Overwhelmed by the sheer excitement, and feeling unable to contain one's emotion, a man of about fifty years, clad in black lacquered armor and holding a long sword with a white hilt, stood upright in the place where he had been seated with a fan. Ise no Saburō Yoshimori, having approached from behind Yūichi, said, "This is a signal; do your duty." Then, Yūichi stepped forward, drew his sword, and shot a straight arrow that struck the nape of the enemy's neck, felling him headlong onto the bottom of the boat. No sound was heard from the Taira side, but on the Minamoto side, archers lowered their quivers, and a murmur arose. Some said, "He has been hit," while others cried, "What a cruel act!" The Taira, perhaps thinking this was not to their liking, formed ranks: one holding a shield, one a bow, and one a long sword; three warriors advanced in a line, raising their shields and calling out, "Come forward, enemies!" The Regent (Gobō) commanded, "There, those young men on strong horses, gallop forth and scatter them!" In response, Mutsu no Kuni's resident Miwaya no Shirō, along with Fujishichi and Jūrō, and Ueno no Kuni's resident Nō no Shirō, and Shinano no Kuni's resident Kiso no Nakaji, led five riders charging forward. From behind the shield's shadow, a painted arrow, tipped with black feathers, was loosed and struck the left chest of Miwaya no Shirō's horse, which was the first to advance, causing it to tumble over like a folding screen. The rider fell, his leg caught in the stirrup, and as he was about to be trampled, he drew his sword. From behind the shield, a large long sword was swung down, and Miwaya no Shirō, thinking, "I cannot withstand this long sword with my small sword," turned and fled. He was pursued immediately. As it seemed he might be struck down by the long sword, he suddenly disappeared, tucked his long sword under his left arm, extended his right hand, and reached for the collar of Miwaya no Shirō's armor. Miwaya no Shirō ran to avoid being caught. He escaped three times, but on the fourth attempt, he was seized. For a moment, he was visible, but then, from the edge of his helmet's plate, he sliced through and escaped. The remaining four riders, unwilling to abandon their horses, stayed behind as spectators. Miwaya no Shirō, having fled to the shadow of his lord's horse, caught his breath. The enemy did not pursue further; instead, leaning on his long sword as a staff, he raised his collar and shouted in a loud voice, "You have heard my voice before; now see me with your own eyes! I am none other than the notorious youth from the capital, Uchisō no Akashichihei Kagekayo!" With this declaration, he turned and departed.

text: 平家是に心地なほして、「惡七兵衞討すな。續けや者共。」とて又二百餘人なぎさに上り、楯を雌羽につき竝べて「敵寄よ。」とぞ招いたる。判官是を見て「安からぬ事なり。」とて、後藤兵衞父子、金子兄弟を先に立て、奧州の佐藤四郎兵衞、伊勢三郎を弓手馬手に立、田代冠者を後に立てゝ、八十餘騎をめいてかけ給へば、平家の兵ども、馬には乘らず、大略歩武者にてありければ、馬に當られじと引退いて、皆船へぞ乘りにける。楯は算を散したる樣に、散散に蹴散さる。源氏の兵共勝に乘て、馬の太腹ひたる程に、打入々々責戰ふ。判官深入して戰ふ程に船の中より熊手を持て、判官の甲の錣に、からり／＼と二三度迄打懸けるを、御方の兵共、太刀長刀で打のけ／＼しける程に、如何したりけん、判官弓をかけ落されぬ。うつぶして鞭をもて掻寄て、取う／＼とし給へば、兵共、「唯捨させ給へ。」と申けれども、終に取て、笑うてぞ歸られける。おとな共、爪彈をして、「口惜き御事候かな。縱千疋萬疋に替させ給べき御寶なりとも、爭か御命に替させ給ふべき。」と申せば、判官、「弓の惜さに取らばこそ。義經が弓といはゞ、二人しても張り、若は三人しても張り、伯父の爲朝が弓の樣ならば、態も落して取すべし。わう弱たる弓を、敵取持て、『是こそ源氏の大將九郎義經が弓よ。』とて嘲哢せんずるが口惜ければ、命に代て取るぞや。」と宣へば、皆人是をぞ感じける。

annotation.translation: The Taira, feeling somewhat relieved, said, 'Do not slay Echi no Bē. Continue, you fellows.' Then again more than two hundred of them disembarked onto the shore, set their shields upright like goose feathers, and stood in formation, shouting, 'Come, enemies!' Thus they summoned them. The Commander (Dagon) saw this and said, 'This is dangerous.' Then he had Goto Bē and his son, and the Kaneko brothers, take the lead, placed Sato Shiro Bē of Mutsu and Ise Saburo on the left and right flanks with bows, set Taira no Kanmuri at the rear, and ordered the remaining eighty-plus horsemen to charge. The Taira soldiers, who were mostly foot soldiers and not mounted, fearing they would be trampled by horses, retreated and all boarded their boats. Their shields were scattered like dice, scattered and trampled about. The Minamoto soldiers, riding triumphantly, pressed forward as their horses grew warm, attacking relentlessly. As the Commander advanced and fought, someone in the boat raised a grappling hook and struck the crest of the Commander's armor two or three times with a clatter. The Commander's own men struck it down with long swords and naginata again and again. Yet somehow, the Commander was not knocked off his horse. Bending forward, he urged his horse with his whip and commanded his men to take the hook. The soldiers pleaded, 'Just let it go, my lord!' but finally he took it. Laughing, he returned. The elders plucked their fingernails and said, 'What a regrettable matter! Even if it were a treasure worth a thousand or ten thousand pieces, would you trade it for your precious life?' The Commander replied, 'If I were to take it out of regret for the bow, that would be one thing. But if it is the bow of Yoshitsune of Minamoto, even two people could draw it, or even three. If it were like the bow of my uncle, Tomoe no Gozen, I might have dropped it and let them take it. But these are such weak bows; if the enemy takes them and says, 'This is indeed the bow of the great general of the Minamoto, Kyūgo Yoshitsune,' and mocks us, that is what I find regrettable. Thus, I take it, even if it costs me my life.' Hearing this, all were moved.
annotation.summary: The Taira, feeling somewhat relieved, said, 'Do not slay Echi no Bē. Continue, you fellows.' Then again more than two hundred of them disembarked onto the shore, set their shields upright like goose feathers, and stood in formation, shouting, 'Come, enemies!' Thus they summoned them. The Commander (Dagon) saw this and said, 'This is dangerous.' Then he had Goto Bē and his son, and the Kaneko brothers, take the lead, placed Sato Shiro Bē of Mutsu and Ise Saburo on the left and right flanks with bows, set Taira no Kanmuri at the rear, and ordered the remaining eighty-plus horsemen to charge. The Taira soldiers, who were mostly foot soldiers and not mounted, fearing they would be trampled by horses, retreated and all boarded their boats. Their shields were scattered like dice, scattered and trampled about. The Minamoto soldiers, riding triumphantly, pressed forward as their horses grew warm, attacking relentlessly. As the Commander advanced and fought, someone in the boat raised a grappling hook and struck the crest of the Commander's armor two or three times with a clatter. The Commander's own men struck it down with long swords and naginata again and again. Yet somehow, the Commander was not knocked off his horse. text: さる程に日暮ければ、平家の船は沖に浮めば源氏は陸に引退いて、むれ高松の中なる野山に、陣をぞ取たりける。源氏の兵共、此三日が間は臥ざりけり。一昨日渡邊福島を出づるとて、其夜大浪にゆられて目睡まず、昨日阿波國勝浦にて軍して終夜中山越え、今日又一日戰くらしたりければ、皆疲果てゝ或は甲を枕にし、或は鎧の袖、箙など枕にして、前後も知らず臥たりけり。其中に、判官と伊勢三郎は寢ざりけり。判官は高き所に登上て、敵や寄ると遠見し給へば、伊勢三郎はくぼき所に隱れ居て、敵寄せば、先づ馬の太腹射んとて待懸たり。平家の方には、能登守を大將にて、其勢五百餘騎夜討にせんと支度しけれども、越中次郎兵衞盛次と、海老次郎守方と先陣を爭ふ程に、其夜も空しくあけにけり。夜討にだにもしたらば源氏なじかはたまるべき。寄せざりけるこそ、責ての運の究めなれ。

annotation.translation: As evening approached, the Heike vessels were anchored in the open sea, while the Genji forces withdrew onto land, establishing their camp among the hills and valleys within the dense stand of tall pines. The Genji soldiers did not sleep for these three days. Having departed from Watanabe no Fushima the day before yesterday, they were tossed by great waves that night and could not close their eyes; yesterday they fought at Katsuura in Awa Province, spent the entire night crossing the Nakayama, and today they have fought another day, and so everyone is utterly exhausted: some using their armor as a pillow, others their breastplates, sleeves, or quivers, unaware of what lies before or behind, they lie down. Among them, Danjo and Ise no Saburō did not sleep. Danjo ascended to a high place to observe from afar whether the enemy were approaching, while Ise no Saburō hid in a low place, waiting to shoot the belly of a horse first should the enemy draw near. On the Heike side, Noto no Kami was appointed as general, and preparations were made to attack them by night with over five hundred riders; however, as Echū no Jirōbē Mori-toki and Ebi no Jirō no Kami Katamichi vied for the vanguard, the night passed without action, and dawn broke in vain. Had they even attempted a night attack, the Genji would surely have been annihilated. The fact that they did not attack signifies that the time for their relentless pursuit has come to an end.

text: 明ければ、平家舟に取乘て當國志度浦へ漕退く。判官三百餘騎が中より馬や人をすぐて八十餘騎、追てぞかゝりける。平家是を見て、「敵は小勢なり。中に取籠て討や。」とて、又千餘人なぎさに上りをめき叫で責戰ふ。さる程に、八島に殘留たる二百餘騎の兵共、後馳に馳來る。平家是を見て、「すはや源氏の大勢の續くは。何十萬騎か有るらん。取籠られては叶ふまじ。」とて又船に取乘て潮に引かれ風に隨て、何くを指共なく、落行ぬ。四國は皆大夫判官に追落されぬ、九國へは入られず、唯中有の衆生とぞ見えし。

annotation.translation: When the tide rose, they boarded the Heike ships and rowed back to Shido-ura in that province. The Gōkan, among his three hundred and more riders, singled out more than eighty riders and horses, and pursued them. Seeing this, the Heike said, 'The enemy is few in number. Let us board them and attack.' Then, again, over a thousand men landed on the beach and shouted loudly, charging into battle. In this way, the two hundred and more soldiers of the Heike who had remained at Yashima came galloping up from the rear. Seeing this, the Heike said, 'Alas, the Minamoto's great force follows behind. How many tens of thousands of riders could there be? If we are boarded, it will not be possible to hold out.' Then, boarding the ships again, they were carried by the current and followed the wind, having no destination in mind, and fell into the sea. The four provinces were all driven back by the Gōkan, they could not enter the nine provinces, and it appeared that only the living beings in the middle were left.

text: 判官志度浦に下居て、頸共實檢しておはしけるが、伊勢三郎義盛をめして、宣ひけるは、「阿波民部重能が嫡子、田内左衞門教能は河野四郎通信が、召せども參らぬを責んとて、三千餘騎にて、伊豫へ越えたりけるが、河野をば打泄して家子郎等百五十人が頸斬て昨日八島の内裏へ參せたりけるが、今日是へ著ときく。汝行向て、ともかくもこしらへて具して參れかし。」と宣へば、畏て承り、旗一流給はてさす儘に、其勢僅に十六騎、皆白裝束にて馳向ふ。義盛教能に行合たり。白旗赤旗、二町許を隔てゝゆらへたり。伊勢三郎義盛使者を立て申けるは「是は源氏の大將軍九郎大夫判官殿の御内に、伊勢三郎義盛と申者で候が、大將に申べき事有て、是まで罷向て候。軍合戰の料でも候はねば、物具もし候はず、弓矢ももたせ候はず、あけて入させ給へ。」と申ければ、三千餘騎の兵共、中を開てぞ通しける。義盛教能に打雙て、「且聞給ても有るらん、鎌倉殿の御弟九郎大夫判官殿院宣を承て、平家追討の爲に、西國へ向はせ給て候が、一昨日阿波國勝浦にて、御邊の伯父櫻間介殿討たれ給ぬ。昨日八島に寄せて御所内裏皆燒拂ひ、大臣殿父子生捕にし奉り能登殿は自害し給ひぬ。その外の君達或は討死に或は海に入り給ひぬ。餘黨の僅に有つるは志度の浦にて、皆討たれぬ。御邊の父阿波民部殿は、降人に參せ給ひて候を、義盛が預り奉て候が、あはれ田内左衞門が是をば夢にも知らで、明日は軍して討れ參らせんずる無慚さよと、通夜歎き給ふが、餘に最愛て此事知らせ奉らんとて是まで罷向て候。其上は軍して討死せんとも降人に參て父を今一度見奉らんともともかうも御邊が計ぞ。」といひければ、田内左衞門、聞ゆる兵なれども運や盡にけん。「且聞く事に少も違ず。」とて、甲を脱弓の弦を弛いて、郎等にもたす。大將がか樣になる上は、三千餘騎の兵ども皆此の如し。僅に十六騎に具せられ、おめおめと降人にこそ參りけれ。「義盛が策誠にゆゝしかりけり。」と判官も感じ給ひけり。やがて田内左衞門をば物具めされて、伊勢三郎に預けらる。「さてあの勢共は如何に。」と宣へば、遠國の者共は、「誰を誰とか思ひ參せ候べき。唯世の亂れをしづめて國を知し召さんを君とせん。」と申ければ、尤然るべしとて、三千餘騎を、皆我勢にぞ具せられける。

annotation.translation: The Danjo (Judge) settled at Sudoura, and after examining the heads, he summoned Ise Sabro Yoshimori and declared: 'Awa no Minbu Shigeno's legitimate son, Taino Saemon Norinori, is Kono Shiro Tsunayoshi's. Though we summoned him, he did not come; therefore, to reprimand him, we crossed over to Iyo with more than three thousand cavalry, defeated Kono, beheaded his retainers, one hundred and fifty men, and their heads, and yesterday we arrived at the Hachiman-no-uchi Inner Palace, but today we hear that they have come here. You go there and, whatever the case, make preparations and come.' When he said this, [Yoshimori] respectfully accepted, and following the command of the flag, only sixteen horsemen, all dressed in white, galloped forth. Yoshimori met Norinori. White flags and red flags waved, separated by about two cho. Ise Sabro Yoshimori sent a messenger to say: 'This is a message from the residence of the Great General of the Minamoto, Ku-no-Daifu Danjo, to Ise Sabro Yoshimori, who is here. I have come this far to report to the General. I am not here for battle, so I have brought no armor, nor do I carry a bow and arrow. Please allow me to enter.' When he said this, the three thousand or more soldiers opened the middle to let him pass. Yoshimori met Norinori and said: 'You may listen for a moment. By the Imperial Decree of His Majesty, the Emperor, the younger brother of the Kamakura Dono, Ku-no-Daifu Danjo, was sent to the Western Provinces to pursue and destroy the Taira. The day before yesterday, at Katsuura in Awa Province, your uncle, Sakurama no Suké, was slain. Yesterday, we landed at Hachiman, burned the Imperial Palace, captured the Dajojin and his son alive, and the Lord of Noto committed suicide. Other lords were either killed in battle or threw themselves into the sea. The remaining remnants were at Sudoura, and all were slain. Your father, Awa no Minbu, surrendered and became a captive, which I took into my custody. Alas, Taino Saemon, unaware of this even in a dream, intends to wage war tomorrow and have his father killed. This is the shamelessness of his lack of remorse. He sighs all night, and because he is so deeply beloved, I have come this far to inform him of this matter. Whether you fight and die, or surrender to see your father once more, it is entirely up to your decision.' When he said this, though Taino Saemon was a soldier, his luck had run out. 'It is no different from what was said,' he declared, took off his armor, loosened his bowstring, and handed it to his retainers. Since the General had taken this course, the three thousand or more soldiers all did the same. Only sixteen men were equipped, and they surrendered sheepishly. 'Yoshimori's stratagem was truly excellent,' the Danjo also thought. Immediately, Taino Saemon was equipped and entrusted to Ise Sabro. 'Now, what of those forces?' he asked. The men from distant provinces replied, 'Whom should we think of as our lord? Let us be the lord who calms the chaos of the world and brings peace to the country.' Thus, it was most appropriate, and the three thousand or more soldiers were all equipped to join our side.

text: 同廿二日辰の刻ばかり渡邊に殘り留たる二百餘艘の船共、梶原を先として、八島の磯にぞ著にける。「四國は皆九郎大夫判官に攻め落されぬ。今は何の用にか逢べき。會に逢ぬ華、六日の菖蒲、いさかひ果てのちぎり哉。」とぞ笑ひける。

annotation.translation: On the twenty-second day, around the hour of the Dragon, the two hundred and more ships that had lingered at Watanabe, led by Kajiwara, came ashore at the rocks of Yashima. "All of Shikoku has been conquered by Lord Goro no Daisuke. What use is it now to meet? A flower that does not meet its companion, the iris of the sixth day, is a promise that has come to an end." Thus he laughed.

Thus he laughed.

text: 判官都を立給ひて後住吉の神主長盛、院の御所へ參て、大藏卿泰經朝臣を以て奏聞しけるは「去十六日の丑刻に當社第三の神殿より、鏑矢の聲出でて、西を指て罷候ぬ。」と申ければ、法皇大に御感有て、御劍已下種々の神寶を長盛して大明神へまゐらせらる。昔神功皇后、新羅を責給ひし時、伊勢大神宮より、二神のあらみさきを差副させ給ひけり。二神御船の艫舳に立て、新羅を安く被責落ぬ。歸朝の後、一神は攝津國住吉の郡に留り給ふ。住吉大明神の御事也。今一神は信濃國諏訪の郡に跡を垂る。諏訪大明神是也。昔の征罰の事を、思食忘ず今も朝の怨敵を滅し給ふべきにやと、君も臣も憑もしうぞ思食されける。

annotation.translation: After the Daimyo departed the capital, the chief priest of Sumiyoshi, Nagamori, went to the Imperial Palace and reported through the Minister of the Great Treasury, Tadaie, that "On the previous day, at the hour of the Ox, a sound like a powder horn was heard from the third shrine of our temple, pointing west, and he has gone." Upon hearing this, the Retired Emperor was greatly moved and, along with his sword, bestowed various divine treasures upon Nagamori to send to the Great Deity. In ancient times, when Empress Jingū was pressing Silla, two gods were dispatched from the Grand Shrine of Ise. The two gods stood at the stern of the imperial boat and brought Silla to submission, allowing it to be easily conquered. After returning to the court, one god remained in the Sumiyoshi district of Settsu Province; this is the matter of the Great Deity of Sumiyoshi. The other god left his trace in the Suwa district of Shinano Province; this is the Great Deity of Suwa. Thinking that the gods of old, who never forgot the matter of the punitive expedition, might now still be annihilating our enemies, both the ruler and his ministers were possessed by them and deeply moved.

text: さる程に、九郎大夫判官義經周防の地に押渡て、兄の參河守と一に成る。平家は長門國ひく島にぞつきにける。源氏阿波國勝浦に著て八島の軍に打勝ぬ。平家引島に著と聞えしかば、源氏は同國の内、追津に著こそ不思議なれ。

annotation.translation: In due course, Kyuro-daijo-danjo Yoshitsune crossed over to the land of Suo and became one with his elder brother, the Sagami-no-kami. The Taira clan settled on Hiku-shima in Nagato Province. The Minamoto clan landed at Katsuura in Awa Province and achieved victory in the battles of the Eight Islands. When it was heard that the Taira clan had landed on Hikeshima, it would have been strange indeed for the Minamoto clan to have landed at Oitsu within the same province.

text: 熊野別當湛増は、平家重恩の身なりしが、忽に其恩を忘れて「平家へや參るべき、源氏へや參るべき。」とて、田邊の新熊野にて御神樂奏して、權現に祈誓し奉る。「唯白旗につけ。」と御託宣有けるを、猶疑なして白い鷄七、赤き鷄七、是を以て權現の御前にて勝負をせさす。赤き鷄一つも勝たず皆負てけり。さてこそ源氏へ參らんと思定めけれ。一門の者共相催し、都合其勢二千餘人、二百餘艘の船に乘り連て、若王子の御正體を船に乘參せ、旗の横上には、金剛童子を書奉て、壇浦へ寄するを見て、源氏も平家も共にをがむ。されども源氏の方へ附ければ、平家興覺てぞ思はれける。又伊豫國の住人、河野四郎通信、百五十艘の兵船に乘連て漕來り、源氏と一つに成にけり。判官旁憑しう力ついてぞ思はれける。源氏の船は三千艘、平家の船は千餘艘、唐船少々相交れり。源氏の勢は重れば、平家の勢は落ぞ行く。

annotation.translation: The Grand Priest of Kumano, Zenzo, had been a man greatly indebted to the Taira, but suddenly he forgot that debt, saying, "Should I go to the Taira, or should I go to the Minamoto?" He played the sacred music at the New Kumano in Tanabe and prayed with an oath to the Gongen. A divine oracle was given: "Only attach the white flag." Still in doubt, he used seven white roosters and seven red roosters to conduct a divination before the Gongen. None of the red roosters won; all lost. Then he resolved to go to the Minamoto. He gathered his clan members; in total, with over two thousand men and over two hundred ships, they embarked, carrying the sacred image of the Prince of Wakamiya onto the ships. On the horizontal crossbar of the flags, they had the image of Kongō Dōji painted and affixed. Seeing them approach Dan-no-ura, both the Minamoto and the Taira marveled. However, when they attached themselves to the side of the Minamoto, the Taira realized their rise. Also, Kono Shiro Tsunamichi, a resident of Iyo Province, came rowing with one hundred and fifty warships and joined the Minamoto. It seemed that the Minamoto's commander was being strongly supported. The Minamoto had three thousand ships, the Taira over one thousand, and a few Chinese ships were intermingled. The Minamoto's forces were heavy, while the Taira's forces were declining.

text: 元歴二年三月廿四日卯刻に、豐前の國の門司赤間關にて、源平矢合とぞ定めける。其日判官と梶原と既に同志軍せんとする事あり。梶原、判官に申けるは「今日の先陣をば、景時にたび候へ。」判官、「義經がなくばこそ。」と宣へば、「大將軍にてこそ在々候へ。」と申ければ、判官、「思ひも寄らず、鎌倉殿こそ大將軍よ。義經は奉行を承たる身なれば、唯殿原と同事ぞ。」と宣へば。梶原、先陣を所望しかねて、「天性此殿は侍の主には成り難し。」とぞつぶやきける。判官、是を聞き「日本一の嗚呼の者哉。」とて、太刀の柄に手をかけ給ふ。梶原「鎌倉殿より外に主を持ぬ者を。」とて、是も太刀の柄に手を懸けり。さる程に嫡子の源太景季、次男平次景高、同三郎景家、父と一所に寄合うたり。判官の氣色を見て、奧州佐藤四郎兵衞忠信、伊勢三郎義盛、源八廣綱、江田源三、熊井太郎、武藏坊辨慶など云ふ一人當千の兵共、梶原を中に取籠て、我討とらんとぞ進ける。されども判官には三浦介取附き奉り、梶原には土肥次郎つかみつき、兩人手を摺て申けるは、「是程の大事を前にかゝへながら、同士軍候はゞ平家力附候なんず。就中、鎌倉殿の還り聞せ給はん處こそ穩便ならず候へ。」と申せば、判官靜まり給ひぬ。梶原進に及ばず。其よりして、梶原、判官を憎みそめて終に讒言して失ひけるとぞ、後には聞えし。

annotation.translation: On the 24th day of the 3rd month of Genryaku Year 2, at the Usagi hour, it was decided that the battle between the Minamoto and Taira would be held at Monji and Akama no Seki in Bungo Province. On that day, there was a plan for the Gon-no-Kami and Kajiwara to already join forces as comrades. Kajiwara said to the Gon-no-Kami, "Let us lead the vanguard today, with the favor of the season." The Gon-no-Kami replied, "It must be Yoshitsune." Kajiwara then said, "It must be the Great General." The Gon-no-Kami answered, "I had not even thought of it; the Kamakura-dono is the Great General. Since Yoshitsune has accepted the role of Gyōji, he is merely a companion of the same rank as the Lord." Hearing this, Kajiwara, unable to desire the vanguard, muttered, "Naturally, this Lord is hard to serve as a retainer." The Gon-no-Kami, upon hearing this, said, "What a remarkable man in all of Japan!" and reached for the hilt of his sword. Kajiwara, saying, "One who has no lord other than the Kamakura-dono," also reached for the hilt of his sword. At that moment, the legitimate son Gen'ei Kagetoki, the second son Heiji Kagetaka, the third son Daisaburō Kageie, and others such as Ōshū Sato Shirōbōei Tadanobu, Ise Saburō Yoshimori, Gen'ya Hirotsuna, Eda Genzō, Kumai Tarō, and Musashibō Benkei, the thousand-man-strong warriors, surrounded Kajiwara and advanced to attack him. However, the Gon-no-Kami was protected by Miura no Suke, and Kajiwara was seized by Doi Jirō. The two, clasping their hands together, said, "While such a great matter is at stake, if we join forces as comrades, the power of the Taira will increase. Especially, it would not be prudent if the Kamakura-dono were to hear of it." Upon hearing this, the Gon-no-Kami fell silent. Kajiwara did not advance. From that time on, Kajiwara came to hate the Gon-no-Kami and eventually slandered him, causing his downfall, as was later heard.

text: さる程に源平兩陣の交ひ海の面卅餘町をぞ隔たる。門司、赤間、壇の浦は、たぎりて落る潮なれば、源氏の船は潮に向うて心ならず押落さる。平家の船は潮に追てぞ出來たる。沖は潮の早ければ、汀に附て、梶原敵の船の行違處に、熊手を打懸て、親子主從十四五人、乘り移り、打物拔で艫舳に散々にないでまはり、分捕數多して、其日の高名の一の筆にぞ附にける。既に、源平兩方陣を合て閧を作る。上は梵天迄も聞え、下は海龍神も驚らんとぞ覺ける。新中納言知盛卿、船の屋形に立出で、大音聲を上て、宣ひけるは「軍は今日ぞ限る。者共少もしりぞく心あるべからず。天竺震旦にも、日本吾朝にも、雙なき名將勇士と云へども、運命盡ぬれば力及ばず。されども名こそ惜けれ。東國の者共に弱氣見ゆな。いつの爲に命をば惜むべき。唯是のみぞ思ふ事。」と宣へば、飛騨三郎左衞門景經御前に候けるが、「是承れ、侍共。」とぞ下知しける。上總惡七兵衞進出て申けるは、「坂東武者は、馬の上でこそ口はきゝ候とも、船軍にはいつ調練し候べき。縱ば魚の木に上たるでこそ候はんずれ。一々に取て海につけ候はん。」とぞ申たる。越中の次郎兵衞申けるは、「同くは大將軍の源九郎に組給へ。九郎は色白うせい小きが、向齒の殊に差出てしるかんなるぞ。但し直垂と鎧を常に著替なれば、きと見分難かん也。」とぞ申ける。上總惡七兵衞申けるは「心こそ猛とも其小冠者何程の事かあるべき。片脇に挾さんで、海へ入れなん物を。」とぞ申たる。新中納言はか樣に下知し給ひ、大臣殿の御まへに參て、「今日は侍共景色よう見え候。但阿波民部重能は、心變したると覺え候。首をはね候はばや。」と申されければ、大臣殿、見えたる事もなうて如何頸をば切るべき。指しも奉公の者であるものを。」「重能參れ。」とて召しければ木蘭地の直垂に、洗革の鎧著て、御前に畏て候。「如何に重能は心替したるか。今日こそ惡う見ゆるぞ。四國の者共に、軍好うせよと下知せよかし。臆したるな。」と宣へば、「なじかは臆し候ふべき。」とて御前を罷立つ。新中納言「あはれきやつが頸を打落さばや。」と思食し、太刀のつかも碎よと握て大臣殿の御方を頻に見給ひけれども、御許され無れば、力及ばず。

annotation.translation: Thus, the two armies of the Minamoto and the Taira were separated by more than thirty cho of the sea's surface. Since the tides at Moji, Akama, and Dan-no-ura were turbulent and falling, the Minamoto ships, facing the tide, were pushed down against their will. The Taira ships had set out with the tide. Since the open sea had a swift current, they approached the shore, and at the place where the enemy ship of Kajiwara Kagemasa passed by, they threw grappling hooks, boarded, and, with fourteen or fifteen father and son, master and retainer, they scattered about the stern, wielding their weapons, and seized many captives, which was recorded as the most famous feat of that day. Already, the two armies of the Minamoto and the Taira clashed, creating a roar. The noise could be heard as high as the heavens, and it was said that even the Dragon King of the Sea below would be startled. Shinchūnagon Tomomori no Kyo, standing up from the ship's cabin, raised his voice and declared: 'The battle is to be decided today. No one among you may show any intention of retreating. Even among the nations of T'ien-chu (India) and Chin-tan (China), and even in our own Japan, if one is called a peerless general or a valiant warrior, when fate runs out, strength is insufficient. Yet, it is a pity to lose one's name. Do not let the people of the Eastern Provinces see you as weak. Why should one cling to one's life? This is the only thing I think of.' When he declared this, Hida no Saburōzaemon Kanesue, who was waiting before His Excellency, gave the order: 'Take this, my retainers.' Then, Kazusa no Akashichiemon advanced and said: 'The warriors of Bandō are used to speaking while on horseback; how could they be trained for naval warfare? Even if they had climbed a fishwood tree, they would still be at a disadvantage. Each one should be placed in the sea.' Then, Echigo no Jirōbeii said: 'Join forces with the great general, Minamoto no Kyūrō. Kyūrō is pale-skinned, slender, and has a prominent front tooth, making him easily recognizable. However, since he always changes his hitatare and armor, it will be difficult to distinguish him.' Then, Kazusa no Akashichiemon said: 'Even if his heart is fierce, what harm could a small boy do? Do not hold him on one side; throw him into the sea.' Shinchūnagon gave such orders, went before the Minister, and said: 'Today, the retainers look very brave. However, Awa no Minbu Shigenou appears to have changed his heart. Would it not be better to cut off his head?' The Minister replied, 'There is no evidence of what he has done; how can I cut off his neck? He is even one of my faithful servants.' Then, 'Shigenou, come here,' he summoned. Shigenou appeared before His Excellency, wearing a mulberry-dyed hitatare and a lacquered armor, standing respectfully. 'How has Shigenou changed his heart? He looks very suspicious today. Order the warriors of the Shikoku region to fight bravely. Do not be cowardly.' When he declared this, Shigenou replied, 'How could I be cowardly?' and then left the presence. Shinchūnagon thought, 'Alas, if I could only cut off his head,' and even tried to break the hilt of his sword in his grip, repeatedly looking toward the Minister, but since the Minister did not grant permission, he was unable to act.

text: 平家は千餘艘を三手に作る。山賀の兵藤次秀遠五百餘艘で先陣に漕向ふ。松浦黨三百餘艘で二陣に續く。平家の君達二百餘艘にて三陣に續き給ふ。兵藤次秀遠は、九國一番の精兵にて有けるが我程こそなけれ共、普通ざまの精兵共五百人をすぐて、舟々の艫舳に立て、肩を一面に比て、五百の矢を一度に放つ。源氏は三千餘艘の船なれば勢の數、さこそ多かりけめども、處々より射ければ何くに精兵有とも見えず。大將軍九郎大夫判官眞先に進で戰ふ。楯も鎧もこらへずして、散散に射しらまさる。平家御方勝ぬとて、頻に攻皷打て悦の鬨をぞ作りける。

annotation.translation: The Heike fleet formed more than a thousand ships into three divisions. The troops of Iwaga, led by Hidetsugu Hidehara, with more than five hundred ships, rowed forward as the vanguard. The Matsuura faction, with more than three hundred ships, followed as the second division. The lords of the Heike, with more than two hundred ships, followed as the third division. Although Hidetsugu Hidehara was the finest soldier of the nine provinces, not quite matching our own caliber, he still selected five hundred elite warriors and stationed them along the sterns of the ships, shoulder to shoulder across the entire deck, and loosed five hundred arrows all at once. Since the Minamoto fleet consisted of more than three thousand ships, their sheer number must have been immense, yet because they shot from various positions, no elite soldiers were visible anywhere. The Great General, Kyūro Daifu no Kanji, advanced first to engage. Neither shields nor armor could withstand the relentless barrage of arrows. Believing the Heike side to be victorious, they repeatedly struck their war drums and raised a cry of triumph.

text: 源氏の方にも和田小太郎義盛、船には乘らず、馬に打乘てなぎさに引へ、甲をば脱いで人にもたせ、鐙の鼻蹈そらし、よ引て射ければ、三町が内との物は外さずつよう射けり。其中に殊に遠う射たると覺しきを、「其矢給はらん。」とぞ招いたる。新中納言是を召寄せて見給へば、白篦に鶴の本白、こうの羽を破合せて作だる矢の十三束二伏有に、沓卷より一束計おいて、和田小太郎平義盛と、漆にてぞ書附たる。平家の方に精兵多しといへども、さすが遠矢射る者は少かりけるやらん、稍久しう有て、伊豫國の住人仁井紀四郎親清召出され、此矢を給はて射返す。是も沖よりなぎさへ三町餘をつと射渡して、和田小太郎が、後一段餘に引へたる三浦の石田左近太郎が弓手のかひなにしたたかにこそ立たりけれ。三浦の人共是を見て、「和田小太郎が、我に過て遠矢射る者なしと思ひて恥かいたるをかしさよ。あれを見よ。」とぞ笑ひける。和田小太郎是を聞き、「やすからぬ事也。」とて小舟に乘て漕出させ、平家の勢の中を差詰め引詰め散々にいければ多の者共射殺れ手負にけり。又判官の乘給る船に、沖より白篦の大矢を一つ射立てゝ、和田が樣に「こまたへ給はらん。」とぞ招いたる。判官此を拔せて見給へば、白篦に山鳥の尾を以て作だりける矢の、十四束三伏あるに、伊豫國の住人仁井紀四郎親清とぞ書附たる。判官後藤兵衞實基を召て、「此矢射つべき者の御方に誰かある。」と宣へば「甲斐源氏に安佐里與一殿こそ、精兵にてましまし候へ。」「さらば呼べ。」とて呼れければ、安佐里の與一出來たり。判官宣ひけるは、「沖より此矢を射て候が、射返せと招き候。御邊あそばし候なんや。」「給はて見候はん。」とて、爪よて、「これは篦が少し弱う候。矢束もちと短う候。同じうは義成が具足にて仕り候はん。」とて、塗籠籐の弓の九尺計あるに、塗篦に黒ほろはいだる矢の、我大手に押握て十五束有けるをうちくはせ、よ引てひやうと放つ。四町餘をつと射渡して、大船の舳に立たる仁井紀四郎親清が眞正中をひやうづばと射て、船底へ逆樣に射倒す。死生をばしらず。安佐里與一は、本より精兵の手きゝ也。二町に走る鹿をば、外さず射けるとぞ聞えし。其後源平、戰に命を惜まずをめき叫んで攻戰ふ。何れ劣れりとも見えず。されども、平家の方には、十善帝王三種の神器を帶して渡らせ給へば、源氏如何あらんずらんとあぶなう思ひけるに、暫は白雲かと覺しくて、虚空に漂ひけるが、雲にては無りけり、主もなき白旗一流舞下て、源氏の船の舳に、竿附の緒のさはる程にぞ見えたりける。判官、「是は八幡大菩薩の現じ給へるにこそ。」と悦で、手水鵜飼をして、是を拜し奉る。兵共皆此のごとし。又源氏の方より江豚といふ魚、一二千這うて、平家の方へぞ向ひける。大臣殿是を御覽じて小博士晴信を召て、「江豚は常に多けれども、未だか樣の事なし。いかゞあるべきと勘へ申せ。」と仰られければ「此江豚見かへり候はば、源氏滅び候べし。はうて通候はば、御方の御軍危う候。」と申も果ねば、平家の船の下を、直にはうて通りけり。「世の中は今はかう。」とぞ申たる。

annotation.translation: To the side of the Genji were Wada no Kotaro Yoshimori, who did not board the boat but mounted a horse, rode it onto the sand, removed his armor and handed it to a man, lowered the stirrups, pulled the bowstring, and shot. Of the three cho within range, he missed none at all. Among them, he felt that he had shot particularly far, so he was summoned, saying, 'Please give me that arrow.' When the new Chūnagon summoned it and examined it, he saw that among the thirteen bundles of arrows, which had been made by breaking and joining the primary white feathers of a crane and the secondary white feathers on a white bamboo arrow fletching, and which were kept in a bundle from the foot-wrap container, there was one bundle written in lacquer with the name 'Wada no Kotaro Taira Yoshimori.' Although the Heike side had many elite soldiers, it seems there were few who could shoot such a long-range arrow. After a considerable delay, Ni no Kijūrō Chikakage, a resident of Iyo Province, was summoned and given the arrow to shoot back. He also shot it from the sea to the shore, covering more than three cho, and Wada no Kotaro, who had pulled back his bow more than one stage further, was the one whose skill was praised by the arch of Shida no Saemon no Taro of Miura. The people of Miura, seeing this, laughed, saying, 'Wada no Kotaro thought there was no one who could shoot a longer arrow than he, and was ashamed; look at that.' Wada no Kotaro, hearing this, said, 'This is not a matter of peace,' and had himself row out in a small boat, pushing through the ranks of the Heike forces, scattering them, and many were shot dead or wounded. Again, at the boat where the Chūgon rode, a single large white bamboo arrow was shot from the sea, and he was summoned, saying, 'Please give me that arrow as well.' The Chūgon drew it out and examined it; it was an arrow made with pheasant tail feathers on a white bamboo fletching, with fourteen bundles and three fathoms, and written in lacquer with the name 'Ni no Kijūrō Chikakage, a resident of Iyo Province.' The Chūgon summoned Goto Bē no Sanezane and said, 'Is there anyone on our side who can shoot this arrow?' 'There is Lord Yasazato Yūichi of the Kōshū Genji, who is an elite soldier,' he replied. 'Then call him.' When he was called, Yasazato's Yūichi appeared. The Chūgon announced, 'An arrow has been shot from the sea to here, and we have been summoned to shoot it back. Will you, my lord, go and handle it?' 'I shall receive it and examine it,' he replied, then drew his fingernail and said, 'This fletching is somewhat weak, and the arrow bundles are a bit short. Let us use the armor of Yoshinari.' He took a lacquered bamboo bow of about nine shaku, inserted an arrow with black horo fletching, which had fifteen bundles and was held in his hand, pulled the bowstring, and shot with a whoosh. He shot it over four cho and more, striking directly the true center of Ni no Kijūrō Chikakage, who stood on the prow of the large boat, and shot him down backward into the hull of the ship. He knew not life or death. Yasazato Yūichi was, from the beginning, a master of elite archery. It is heard that he never missed a deer running two cho away. After this, the Genji and the Heike, sparing no life in battle, shouted and attacked one another. Neither side appeared inferior. However, the Heike side, having crossed over with the Tenzen Teiō and the Three Sacred Treasures, the Genji wondered what they could do, feeling a deep anxiety. Then, for a while, they thought it was a white cloud drifting in the void, but it was not a cloud; a white banner without a lord flew down, and when it came close enough to the prow of the Genji's boat to touch the rope attached to the pole, it was seen. The Chūgon, rejoicing, said, 'This must be the manifestation of the Great Bodhisattva Hachiman!' and performed the water-purification ritual, bowing and offering worship to it. The soldiers were all like this. Again, from the Genji side, one or two thousand sea otters swam forth, heading toward the Heike side. The Daimyō, seeing this, summoned the Little Scholar Harunobu and said, 'Sea otters are often numerous, but never have such things happened before. What do you think should be done?' He was told, 'If these sea otters turn back, the Genji will be destroyed; if they pass through, your forces will be in danger.' But they did not turn back; instead, they passed straight through beneath the Heike's ships. 'The world is now like this,' he said.

text: 阿波民部重能は、此三箇年が間、平家に能々忠を盡し、度々の合戰に命を惜まず防ぎ戰ひけるが、子息田内左衞門を生捕にせられて、いかにも叶はじとや思ひけん、忽に心替りして、源氏に同心してんげり。平家の方にははかりごとに、好き人をば兵船に乘せ、雜人共を唐船に乘せて、源氏心にくさに唐船を攻めば、中に取籠て討んと支度せられたりけれども、阿波民部が囘忠の上は、唐船には目も懸けず、大將軍のやつし乘給へる兵船をぞ攻たりける。新中納言「やすからぬ、重能めを切て棄べかりつるものを。」と千たび後悔せられけれども叶はず。さる程に四國鎭西の兵共、皆平家を背いて、源氏に附く。今まで從ひ著たりし者共も君に向て弓を引き、主に對して太刀を拔く。彼岸につかんとすれば、波高して叶ひ難し。此の汀に寄らんとすれば、敵箭鋒を汰て待懸たり。源平の國爭、今日を限とぞ見えたりける。

annotation.translation: Awa no Minbu Shigenori, during these three years, had served the Taira clan with utmost loyalty and, in repeated battles, had not spared his life in defense, but when his son Taino Saemon was captured alive, he must have thought, 'It is impossible,' and suddenly changed his heart, joining the Minamoto clan. On the Taira side, they had planned to put their favorite people on warships and commoners on Tang ships, intending to attack the Tang ships to cause trouble for the Minamoto, and had prepared to capture and kill those inside. However, due to Awa no Minbu's return to loyalty, he did not even cast a glance at the Tang ships, but attacked the warship on which the Great General was riding. The New Chancellor said, 'It is not peaceful; if only I had cut off Shigenori's head and discarded it!' and repented a thousand times, but it was no use. In this way, the soldiers of Shikoku and Saikoku, all turned away from the Taira and joined the Minamoto. Even those who had previously followed and served the clan now drew their bows against their lord and drew their swords against their master. If they wished to reach the other shore, the waves were high and it was difficult to accomplish; if they wished to approach this shore, they had to wait under the cutting edge of enemy arrows. It seems that the national conflict between the Genji and the Heike has reached its limit today.

text:
源氏の兵共既に平家の船に乘移りければ、水主梶取共、射殺され、切殺されて船を直すに及ばず、船底に倒伏しにけり。新中納言知盛卿、小船に乘て、御所の御船に參り、「世の中はいまはかうと見えて候。見苦しからん物共皆海へ入させ給へ。」とて艫舳に走り廻り、掃いたり拭うたり、塵拾ひ、手づから掃除せられけり。女房達、「中納言殿、軍は如何に。」と口々に問ひ給へば、「めづらしき東男をこそ御覽ぜられ候はんずらめ。」とて、から／＼と笑ひ給へば、「何條の只今の戲れぞや。」とて、
聲々にをめき叫給ひけり。二位殿は此有樣を御覽じて日比思食設けたる事なれば、に
ぶ色の二衣打覆き、練袴の傍高く挾み、伸璽を脇に挾み、寶劔を腰にさし、主上を抱
奉て、「我身は女なりとも、敵の手にはかゝるまじ。君の御供に參る也。御志思ひ參
せ給はん人々は、急ぎ續き給へ。」とて舟端へ歩み出られけり。主上は今年は八歳に
成せ給へども御年の程より遙にねびさせ給ひて、御容美しくあたりも照り輝くばかり
也。御ぐし黒う優々として御せなかすぎさせ給へり。あきれたる御樣にて、「尼ぜ、
我をばいづちへ具してゆかんとするぞ。」と仰ければ、幼き君に向奉り涙を押へて申
されけるは、「君は未知し召れさぶらはずや。先世の十善戒行の御力に依て、今萬乘
の主と生させ給へども、惡縁に引かれて、御運既に盡させ給ひぬ。先づ東に向はせ給
ひて、伊勢大神宮に御暇申させ給ひ、其後西方淨土の來迎に預らむと思食し、西に向はせ給ひて御念佛候ふべし。此國は粟散邊地とて、心憂き境にてさぶらへば、極樂淨土とてめでたき處へ具し參せさぶらふぞ。」と泣々申させ給へば、山鳩色の御衣にびんづら結せ給ひて、御涙におぼれ、小さく美しき御手を合せて先東を伏し拜み、伊勢大神宮に御暇申させ給ひ、其後西に向はせ給ひて、御念佛有しかば、二位殿やがて抱き奉り、「浪のしたにも、都のさぶらふぞ。」と慰奉て千尋の底へぞ入給ふ。悲き哉、無常の春の風、忽に華の御容を散し、無情哉、分段の荒き浪、玉體を沈め奉る。殿をば長生と名附けて長き棲かと定め、門をば不老と號して、老せぬとざしとかきたれども、未だ十歳の内にして、底の水くづとならせ給ふ。十善帝位の御果報、申すも中々愚なり。雲上の龍降て、海底の魚となり給ふ。大梵高臺の閣の上、釋提喜見の宮の内、古は槐門棘路の間に九族を靡かし、今は舟の中波の下に、御命を一時に亡し給ふこそ悲しけれ。

annotation.translation: The Minamoto forces had already transferred to the Taira ships, so the boatmen and rowers were shot dead and cut down, and there was no time to repair the ships; they fell prostrate on the ship's bottom. The newly appointed Chancellor, Prince Tomomori, boarded a small boat and went to the Imperial Palace's ship, saying, "The world now appears thus. Let all those who are shameful be cast into the sea." He ran back and forth along the stern and bow, sweeping and wiping, picking up dust, and personally cleaning. The female attendants, asking in unison, "My Lord Chancellor, what of the army?" he replied, "You are surely gazing upon some strange Eastern man," and laughed heartily. They cried out in unison, "What manner of mere jest is this?" and all began to weep and scream. Lady Ni no Taimyō, having seen this scene, was already filled with sorrow; she wore two layers of dull-colored robes, tucked her training hakama high, held her sword at her side, strapped her treasure sword to her waist, embraced the Sovereign, and said, "Though I am a woman, I will not fall into the enemy's hands. I shall accompany His Majesty. Those who wish to follow your will, hasten and follow." She then walked to the edge of the boat. Although the Sovereign had reached the age of eight this year, he appeared far older than his years, his countenance so beautiful that it seemed to illuminate everything around him. His black hair was thick and graceful, and his neck was slender. With such a remarkable appearance, he said, "Nun, you intend to take me to the earth?" Turning to the young Sovereign, she held back her tears and replied, "Has His Majesty not yet understood? By the power of the Ten Precepts of Good Conduct from a previous life, you have been born as the ruler of ten thousand chariots, but drawn by evil karma, your fortune has already come to an end. First, turn eastward and seek permission from the Grand Shrine of Ise; thereafter, turning westward, you should hope to welcome the descent to the Pure Land of the West. This land is called a distant land of millet grains, a place of sorrow where we reside; thus, we shall go to the blissful place of the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss." She said this while weeping. Clad in a robe the color of mountain doves, she was wrapped in her sorrow, clasped her small, beautiful hands together, bowed her head toward the east, sought permission from the Grand Shrine of Ise, then turned westward and recited the Nembutsu. Lady Ni no Taimyō immediately embraced him, saying, "Even in the depths of the waves, we serve the capital," and comforted him as they entered the thousand-fathom depths. Oh, how sorrowful! The impermanent spring wind suddenly scattered the flower-like countenance. Oh, how merciless! The rough waves of the segmented ocean submerged the jade body. They named the palace "Eternal Life" and designated the residence as "Ageless," inscribing that it would never age, yet within ten years, he was turned to water at the bottom of the sea. The fruit of the Ten Precepts of the Emperor is indeed foolish to speak of. The dragon descending from the clouds becomes a fish at the ocean's bottom. Once, atop the high tower of the Great Brahma, within the palace of Sakra, he made the nine clans bow in the midst of locust-gate and thorny paths; now, in the boat, beneath the waves, it is truly sorrowful that his life was lost in an instant.

text: 女院は此御有樣を御覽じて、御燒石、御硯左右の御懷に入て、海へ入せ給ひたりけるを、渡邊黨に源五馬允眤誰とは知り奉らねども、御髮を熊手に懸て、引上奉る。女房達、「あな淺まし、あれは女院にて渡らせ給ぞ。」と聲々口々に申されければ、判官に申て急ぎ御所の御舟へわたし奉る。大納言佐殿は、内侍所の御唐櫃をもて、海へ入らんとし給ひけるが、袴の裾を舟端にいつけられ、蹴纒ひて倒れ給たりけるを、兵ども取留め奉る。さて武士共内侍所の御唐櫃の鎖をねぢ切て、既に御蓋を開かんとすれば忽に目くれ鼻血垂る。平大納言、生捕にせられておはしけるが、「あれは内侍所の渡らせ給ふぞ。凡夫は見奉らぬ事ぞ。」と宣へば、兵共みなのきにけり。其後判官平大納言に申合せて、本の如く緘げ納め奉る。

annotation.translation: The Lady-in-Waiting, having viewed this manner of the Emperor, placed the burning stones and the inkstone, left and right, into her bosom, and entered the sea, but the Watanabe party, though they did not know who the Lord Gen was, caught her hair with a bear-claw and pulled her up. The ladies-in-waiting said, "Oh, how shallow! That is the Lady-in-Waiting, let her be passed!" speaking in unison, and reported to the Judge, who quickly had her transferred to the imperial boat. The Minister of the Right, Sa-no-Dono, attempted to enter the sea with the imperial chest of the Palace Women's Office, but his hakama hem was caught by the boat's edge, and he stumbled and fell. The soldiers detained him. Then the warriors twisted and broke the lock of the imperial chest of the Palace Women's Office, and were about to open the lid, when suddenly he bled from the nose and his eyes rolled back. The Minister of the Right, Hei, who had been taken alive, said, "That is to be passed over by the Palace Women's Office. It is not for ordinary men to see." Upon hearing this, the soldiers all withdrew. After that, the Judge and the Minister of the Right, Hei, conferred, and as before, they sealed and stored it.
