text: さる程に門脇平中納言教盛卿、修理大夫經盛、兄弟鎧の上に碇を負ひ、手に手を取組んで海へぞ入給ひける。小松の新三位中將資盛、同少將有盛、從弟左馬頭行盛、手に手を取組んで一所に沈み給ひけり。人々はか樣にし給へども、大臣殿父子は海に入んずる氣色もおはせず、舟端に立出でて四方見回し、あきれたる樣にておはしけるを、侍共あまりの心憂さに、そばを通る樣にて、大臣殿を海へつき入奉る。右衞門督是を見てやがて飛入給けり。皆人は、重き鎧の上に重き物を負うたり抱いたりして入ればこそ沈め。此人親子はさもし給はぬ上憖に究竟の水練にておはしければ、しづみもやり給はず。大臣殿は、「右衞門督沈まば我も沈まむ、助かり給はゞ我も助らむ。」と思ひ給ふ。右衞門督も「父しづみ給はゞ吾もしづまむ、助かり給はば我もたすからむ。」と思ひて、互に目を見かはし游ぎありき給ふ程に、伊勢三郎義盛、小船をつと漕寄せ、先づ右衞門督を、熊手に懸て引上げ奉る。大臣殿、是を見ていよ／＼沈みもやり給はねば同う取奉てけり。

annotation.translation: Thus, the Gate-side Minister-Advisor Taira no Motomori and the Minister of Works, Kane-mori, brothers, bore their armor on their backs and, holding hands, entered the sea. The newly promoted Third Rank Minister of the Left, Tomomori, and his younger brother, the Junior Captain Arimori, along with their first cousin, the Captain of the Left Stable, Yukimori, also held hands and sank together. People were greatly moved, but the Minister and his son showed no sign of entering the sea; instead, they stood at the stern of the boat, looking about in a bewildered manner. The attendants, overcome with sorrow, approached and pushed the Minister into the sea. The Right Guard Captain saw this and immediately leaped in. Everyone, burdened with heavy armor and heavy objects, sank as they entered. But these father and son, being thoroughly trained in swimming, did not sink at all. The Minister thought, "If the Right Guard Captain sinks, I will sink too; if he is saved, I will be saved." The Right Guard Captain thought, "If my father sinks, I will sink; if he is saved, I will be saved." While they gazed at each other and played in the water, Ise no Saburō Yoshimori rowed a small boat swiftly, first hoisting the Right Guard Captain up with a bear-pole and pulling him aboard. Seeing this, the Minister, refusing to sink any longer, was also taken aboard together.

text: 大臣殿の御乳母飛騨三郎左衞門景經、小船に乘て、義盛が船に乘移り、「吾君取奉るは何者ぞ。」とて太刀を拔で走りかゝる。義盛既にあぶなう見えけるを、義盛が童、主を討せじと中に隔たり、景經に打てかゝる。景經が打つ太刀に、義盛が童、甲の眞甲打破れて、二の太刀に頸打落されぬ。義盛猶あぶなう見えけるを、並の船より、堀彌太郎親經、よ引いて兵と射る。景經内甲を射させてひるむ處を、堀彌太郎、義盛が船に乘移て、三郎左衞門に組で伏す。堀が郎等主に續いて乘移り、景經が鎧の草摺引上て、二刀刺す。飛騨三郎左衞門景經聞ゆる大力の剛の者なれども運や盡にけん。痛手は負つ、敵はあまたあり、そこにて終に討たれにけり。大臣殿は生ながら取りあげられ目の前で乳子がうたるるを見給ふに、いかなる心ちかせられけん。

annotation.translation: The Great Minister's wet nurse, Hida Saburōzaemon Kanesue, boarded a small boat, transferred to Yoshimori's boat, and said, 'Who is it that takes my lord?' as he drew his sword and rushed forward. Yoshimori, seeing that it was dangerous, had his young servant stand between them to prevent the master from being killed; the servant attacked Kanesue. With Kanesue's sword strike, Yoshimori's servant had his armor pierced through the main breastplate, and with a second strike his neck was cut off. Yoshimori still appeared to be in danger, but from an adjacent boat, Hori Yatarō Chiketsuna pulled him back and shot arrows. While Kanesue, having been shot in his inner armor, faltered, Hori Yatarō transferred to Yoshimori's boat and grappled with Saburōzaemon. Hori's retainers followed their master onto the boat; Kanesue's armor skirt was lifted, and he was stabbed with two swords. Although Hida Saburōzaemon Kanesue was known as a man of great strength and prowess, his luck had run out. He suffered heavy wounds, his enemies were many, and there he was finally killed. The Great Minister was taken alive while still breathing, and when he saw the wet nurse struck down before his eyes, what sorrow must he have felt.

text: 凡そ能登守教經の矢先に廻る者こそ無りけれ。矢種の有る程射盡して今日を最後とや思はれけん、赤地の錦の直垂に、唐綾威の鎧著て、いか物作りの大太刀拔、白柄の大長刀の鞘をはづし、左右に持て、なぎ廻り給ふに面を合する者ぞなき、多の者ども討たれにけり。新中納言使者を立てゝ、「能登殿、痛う罪な作り給ひそ。さりとて好き敵か。」と宣ひければ、「さては大將軍に組めごさんなれ。」と心得て、打物莖短に取て、源氏の船に乘り移り、をめき叫んで責戰ふ。されども判官を見知給はねば、物具の好き武者をば「判官か」と目を懸て、馳囘り給ふ。判官も先に心得て面に立つ樣にしけれども、兎かく違ひて、能登殿には組れず。されども如何したりけん。判官の船に乘當て「あはや」と目を懸て飛でかゝるに、判官叶はじとや思はれけん、長刀脇にかい挾み、御方の船の二丈ばかりのいたりけるに、ゆらりと飛乘り給ひぬ。能登殿は疾態や劣られけん。やがて續いても飛び給はず。今はかうと思はれければ太刀長刀海へ投入れ、甲も脱で棄られけり。鎧の草摺かなぐり棄て、胴ばかり著て、大童になり、大手を廣げて立たれたり。凡當を撥てぞ見えたりける。怖しなども愚也。能登殿大音聲を上て、「我と思はん者共は寄て教經に組で生捕にせよ。鎌倉へ下て頼朝に逢て物一言云はんと思ふぞ。よれやよれ。」と宣へども寄る者一人も無りけり。こゝに土佐國の住人、安藝の郷を知行しける安藝大領實康が子に、安藝太郎實光とて、三十人が力持たる大力の剛の者あり。我にちとも劣らぬ郎等一人、弟の次郎も、普通にはすぐれたるしたゝか者也。安藝太郎能登殿を見奉て申けるは、「如何に心猛くましますとも我等三人取付たらんに縱長十丈の鬼なりとも、などか從へざるべき。」とて主從三人小船に乘て、能登殿の船に押竝べ、えいといひて乘移り甲のしころを傾け太刀を拔て一面に打て懸る。能登殿ちとも噪ぎ給はず、眞先に進だる安藝太郎が郎等をすそを合せて、海へどうと蹴入給ふ。續いてよる安藝太郎を、弓手の脇に取て挾み、弟の次郎をば、馬手の脇にかい挾み、一しめしめて、「いざうれ、さらば己等死出の山の供せよ。」とて、生年廿六にて、海へつとぞ入給ふ。

annotation.translation: It is likely that those who turned to meet the arrow of the Governor of Noto, Kanezane, were the very ones who, having shot their arrows to the end until today, thought, 'Let this be the last,' wearing a red damascene hitatare and a Tang-style lacquered armor, drawing a great long sword from its scabbard, holding it in both hands, and swinging it around with no one able to face him, many were defeated. Sending a messenger to the new Chūnagon, they said, 'Lord Noto, do not commit such a grievous crime. Yet, are you fond of your enemies?' Upon hearing this, thinking, 'Then I must engage the Great General,' they shortened the hilt of their weapon, boarded a Minamoto ship, and, wailing and shouting, pressed the attack. However, since they did not recognize the Gōken, they would gaze upon the warriors adorned with their gear, thinking, 'Is that the Gōken?' and charge around. The Gōken, having anticipated this, positioned himself to face them, but they were mistaken and failed to engage Lord Noto. Yet, what could be done? As they boarded the Gōken's ship, crying 'Aha!' and leaping forward, the Gōken, thinking, 'I cannot allow this,' tucked his long sword to his side, and when they reached the other side of his ship, about two zhang away, they leaped onto it with a sway. Lord Noto must have been greatly distressed, yet they did not continue leaping. Thinking now that this was the case, they cast their swords and long blades into the sea, removed their armor, and discarded it. They threw aside the grass-skirt of their armor, wearing only the cuirass, became like young boys, spread their arms, and stood. Only their upper bodies were visible. Fear is foolishness. Lord Noto raised his voice and declared, 'All who think they are me, come and engage Kanezane and capture him alive! I intend to descend to Kamakura and meet Yoritomo to say a few words. Come, come!' Yet not a single person approached. Here, among the residents of Tosa Province, there was a man named Anji no Gōri, Sanezane, who held the estate of Anji no Sato. His son, Anji no Taro, Sanemitsu, was one of thirty men of great strength and might. He was a retainer who was not inferior to me, and his younger brother, the Second Son, was also outstanding in ordinary times. When Anji no Taro saw Lord Noto, he said, 'No matter how fierce your heart may be, if we three attack you, even if you were a ghost ten jō long, how could you not submit?' Thus, the lord and his two retainers boarded a small boat, lined up alongside Lord Noto's ship, shouted 'Ei!' and boarded, tilting their armor, drew their swords, and struck all around. Lord Noto did not stir at all. He kicked the retainer of Anji no Taro, who was advancing foremost, into the sea, holding his hem. Then, taking the archer's side, he embraced the archer, and holding the Second Son by the horseman's side, with one final shout, 'Come, let us go! Then you shall accompany me to the mountain of death!' he plunged into the sea, having lived twenty-six years.

text: 新中納言、「見べき程の事は見つ、今は自害せん。」とて、乳人子の伊賀平内左衞門家長を召て「いかに日比の約束は違まじきか。」と宣へば、「子細にや及候。」と申。中納言に、鎧二領著せ奉り、我身も鎧二領著て、手を取組で海へぞ入にける。是を見て侍共廿餘人後たてまつらじと手に手を取組で一所に沈みけり。其中に、越中次郎兵衞、上總五郎兵衞、惡七兵衞、飛騨四郎兵衞は、何としてか逃れたりけん、そこをも又落にけり。海上には赤旗赤幟共、投捨かなぐり捨たりければ、龍田川の紅葉葉を、嵐の吹散したるがごとし。汀に寄る白浪も、薄紅にぞ成にける。主もなき虚しき船は、潮に引かれ風に從て、いづくを指ともなくゆられゆくこそ悲しけれ。生捕には、前内大臣宗盛公、平大納言時忠、右衞門督清宗、内藏頭信基、讃岐中將時實、兵部少輔雅明、大臣殿の八歳になり給ふ若公、僧には二位僧都專親、法勝寺執行能圓、中納言律師仲快、經誦坊阿闍梨融圓、侍には源大夫判官季貞、攝津判官盛澄、橘内左衞門季康、藤内左衞門信康、阿波民部重能父子、以上三十八人也。菊池次郎高直、原田大夫種直は、軍以前より郎等共相具して降人に參る。女房達には、女院、北の政所、廊御方、大納言佐殿、帥佐殿、治部卿局以下、四十三人とぞ聞えし[2]元歴二年の春の暮、如何なる年月にて一人海底に沈み、百官波上に浮らん。國母官女は、東夷西戎の手に從ひ、臣下卿相は數萬の軍旅にとらはれて、舊里に歸り給ひしに、或は朱買臣が錦をきざる事を歎き、或は王昭君が胡國に赴きし恨も、かくやとぞ悲み給ひける。

annotation.translation: The new Chūnagon said, 'There is much to see; now I shall commit suicide.' He summoned Iga Taira no Saemon Nagamasa, the wet-nurse's son, and said, 'How could I possibly break the promise made at Hibi?' Nagamasa replied, 'I will follow your instructions.' The Chūnagon donned two suits of armor, donned two suits of armor himself, took hold of each other's hands, and plunged into the sea. Witnessing this, more than twenty retainers took each other's hands and sank together. Among them, Echizen no Jirōbē, Shimōsa no Gorōbē, Akushichi Bē, and Hida no Shirobē—how could they possibly escape? They too fell into the sea. The red flags and red banners were thrown and scattered upon the sea, resembling autumn maple leaves blown about by a storm. The white waves breaking upon the shore also turned a pale crimson. The empty, ownerless ship, drawn by the tide and following the wind, swayed aimlessly toward nowhere—how sorrowful. As for those taken alive: the former Dainagon Mochimori, the Taira Dainagon Tokitada, the Uemon-no-Kami Kiyomune, the Kurōdono Nobumoto, the Sanuki no Shō Tokumi, the Hyōbu-no-Shō Masakiyo, His Excellency the Minister's eight-year-old young prince; the monks: the Niji Sōzu Senkin, the Hōshō-ji Shōzu Nōen, the Chūnagon Ritsushi Nakaka, the Kyōshōbō Ajari Yūen; the samurai: the Gen no Daifu Hankei Motosada, the Settsu no Daifu Morisumi, the Tachibana no Saemon Monokuni, the Fuji no Saemon Nobuyasu, the Awaji no Minbu Shigenō and his son; in all, thirty-eight persons. Kikuchi no Jirō Takanao and Harada no Daifu Tananao descended with their attendants, having prepared themselves since before the battle. As for the ladies-in-waiting: the retired Empress, the Kitano no Masu-jo, the Rōgo no Kata, the Dainagon no Sa-jo, the Sō-shō no Sa-jo, the Jibu-kyō no Tsubone and below, totaling forty-three persons. In the twilight of spring, the second year of Genryaku, how many years passed before one sank to the bottom of the sea, while the hundred officials floated upon the waves? The imperial mother and palace women fell into the hands of the Eastern barbarians and Western tribes, while ministers and high officials were captured by tens of thousands of soldiers; though they returned to their old homes, some lamented that they could not wear the brocade of Zhu Maichen, while others mourned the sorrow of Wang Zhaojun departing for the barbarian lands, as if they were saying, 'Is this how it will be?'

As for those taken alive: the former Dainagon Mochimori, the Taira Dainagon Tokitada, the Uemon-no-Kami Kiyomune, the Kurōdono Nobumoto, the Sanuki no Shō Tokumi, the Hyōbu-no-Shō Masakiyo, His Excellency the Minister's eight-year-old young prince; the monks: the Niji Sōzu Senkin, the Hōshō-ji Shōzu Nōen, the Chūnagon Ritsushi Nakaka, the Kyōshōbō Ajari Yūen; the samurai: the Gen no Daifu Hankei Motosada, the Settsu no Daifu Morisumi, the Tachibana no Saemon Monokuni, the Fuji no Saemon Nobuyasu, the Awaji no Minbu Shigenō and his son; in all, thirty-eight persons. Kikuchi no Jirō Takanao and Harada no Daifu Tananao descended with their attendants, having prepared themselves since before the battle. As for the ladies-in-waiting: the retired Empress, the Kitano no Masu-jo, the Rōgo no Kata, the Dainagon no Sa-jo, the Sō-shō no Sa-jo, the Jibu-kyō no Tsubone and below, totaling forty-three persons. In the twilight of spring, the second year of Genryaku, how many years passed before one sank to the bottom of the sea, while the hundred officials floated upon the waves? The imperial mother and palace women fell into the hands of the Eastern barbarians and Western tribes, while ministers and high officials were captured by tens of thousands of soldiers; though they returned to their old homes, some lamented that they could not wear the brocade of Zhu Maichen, while others mourned the sorrow of Wang Zhaojun departing for the barbarian lands, as if they were saying, 'Is this how it will be?'

text: 同四月三日、九郎大夫判官義經、源八廣綱を以て、院の御所へ奏聞せられけるは、去三月二十四日、豐前國田浦門司關、長門國壇浦赤間關にて、平家を責め落し三種神器事故なう返し入れ奉るの由、申されたりければ、院中の上下騒動す。廣綱を御坪の内へ召し、合戰の次第を委しう御尋ありて、御感のあまり左兵衞尉に成されけり。「一定内侍所返り入らせ給ふか、見て參れ。」とて、五日、北面に候ける藤判官信盛を西國へ差遣はさる。宿所へも歸らず、やがて院の御馬を給はて鞭を擧げ、西をさしてぞ馳下る。

annotation.translation: On the third day of the fourth month of that year, it was reported to the Imperial Palace by Kurōdaijo no Gogen, Yoshitsune, using Minamoto no Hirotsuna, that on the twenty-fourth day of the third month of the preceding year, at the Tomura Gate Guard in Bungo Province and the Dan-no-ura Akama Gate Guard in Nagato Province, the Taira clan had been defeated and the Three Sacred Treasures were about to be returned. Because this was reported, the entire court was thrown into confusion. Hirotsuna was summoned into the inner quarters of the Imperial Palace, and the details of the battle were thoroughly inquired into by the Emperor, who, overwhelmed with emotion, appointed him to the post of Saemon-no-Suke. 'Certainly, have the Lady-in-Waiting's quarters returned,' he said, 'and go and see.' Thus, on the fifth day, Fujinō no Nobumori, who had been waiting in the Northern Face, was dispatched to the Western Provinces. He did not return to his lodging; instead, he immediately received the Emperor's horse, raised his whip, and galloped off toward the west.

text: 同十四日、九郎大夫判官義經、平氏男女の生捕共相具して上りけるが、播磨國明石浦にぞ著にける。名を得たる浦なれば、深行くまゝに月すみ上り、秋の空にもおとらず。女房達差つどひて、「一年是を通りしには、かゝるべしとは思はざりき。」などいひて、忍音に泣合れけり。帥佐殿つくづく月を詠め給ひ、いと思ひ殘す事もおはせざりければ、涙に床も浮くばかりにて、かうぞ思ひ續け給ふ。

annotation.translation: On the fourteenth day of the same month, Kurogodaibu no Gon no Gon Yoshitsune and others of the Taira men and women, all captured alive, went up, and they arrived at Akashi-ura in Harima Province. Since it was a bay known by name, the moon rose deeply into the night, not losing its brilliance even in the autumn sky. The female attendants gathered and said, "When we passed through here last year, we did not think it would be like this," and they wept together in hushed tones. The Shoshi-dono deeply chanted poems about the moon, and since there was nothing he left unfulfilled in his heart, the bed seemed to float in tears, and thus he continued to think so.

text: 「さこそ物悲しう昔戀しうもおはしけめ。」と判官猛き武士なれども、情ある男士なれば、身に染て哀にぞ思はれける。

annotation.translation: "How sorrowful and how longing for the past it must have been." Although the Dango was a fierce warrior, because he was a man with feelings, he was deeply moved to sorrow.

text: 同二十五日、内侍所、璽の御箱、鳥羽に著せ給ふと聞えしかば、内裏より御迎に參らせ給ふ人々、勘解由小路中納言經房卿、高倉宰相中將泰通、權右中辨兼忠、左衞門權佐親雅、榎並中將公時、但馬少將教能、武士には伊豆藏人大夫頼兼、石河判官代能兼、左衞門尉有綱とぞ聞えし。其夜の子刻に、内侍所、璽の御箱、太政官の廳に入せ給。寶劔は失にけり。神璽は海上に浮びたりけるを、片岡太郎經春が、取上奉たりけるとぞきこえし。

annotation.translation: On the same twenty-fifth day, when it was heard that the Inner Palace, the Imperial Seal and its box, were being conveyed to Toba, people came from the Inner Palace to welcome them: Kanegon Nakagong Tadafusa, Takakura Shō no Shō Taitsū, Gon Ujinaka no Ben Kanesada, Saemon Gonsa Tomomasa, Enami Shō no Shō Kintoki, Tajima Shō no Shō Nōnori; among the warriors were Izu Kurō no Daifu Yorikane, Ishikawa Hangan Dai Nōken, and Saemon Jō Aritsuna. That night, in the hour of the rat, the Inner Palace and the Imperial Seal and its box were conveyed into the office of the Daijōkan. The sacred sword was lost. It was heard that the sacred jewel had floated on the sea, and Katakura Taro Noriharu had retrieved it.

text: 吾朝には神代より傳はれる靈劍三あり。十握劍、天の早切劍、草薙劍是也。十握劍は大和國磯上布留社に納めらる。天早切の劍は尾張國熱田宮にありとかや。草薙劍は内裏にあり。今の寶劍是也。此劍の由來を申せば、昔、素盞烏尊出雲國曾我里に宮造りし給ひしに其處に八色の雲常に立ちければ、尊是を御覽じてかくぞ詠じ給ひける。

annotation.translation: In our age there are three divine swords transmitted from the age of the gods: the Totsuka-no-Tsurugi, the Ama-no-Habakiri, and the Kusano-Tsurugi. The Totsuka-no-Tsurugi is enshrined at the Iwaki-Furu Shrine in Yamato Province; the Ama-no-Habakiri is said to be at the Atsuta Shrine in Owari Province; and the Kusano-Tsurugi is in the Inner Palace. text: 是を三十一文字の始とす。國を出雲と名付る事も即ちこの故とぞ承る。

annotation.translation: This is taken as the beginning of the thirty-one characters. I have heard that the reason for naming the country Izumo is also precisely this.

text: 昔、尊、出雲國ひの河上に下り給ひし時國津の神に足なつち、手なつちとて夫神婦神おはします。其子に端正の娘あり。稻田姫と號す。親子三人泣居たり。尊「如何に」と問ひ給へば答へ申ていはく、「我に娘八人ありき。皆大蛇の爲にのまれぬ。今一人殘るところの少女又呑れんとす。件の大蛇、尾首共に八つあり。各八の峯八の谷に這はびこれり。靈樹異草背に生ひたり。幾千年を歴たりといふ事を知らず。眼は日月の光の如し。年々に人を呑む。親呑まるるものは子悲み、子呑まるゝものは親悲み、村南村北に哭する聲絶えずとぞ申ける。尊哀に思食し、此少女をゆつのつまぐしに取なし、御ぐしに差藏させ給ひ、八の舟に酒を入れ、美女の姿を造て高き岡に立つ。其影酒にうつれり。大蛇人と思ひて其影を飽まで飮で醉臥たりけるを尊帶給へる十握の劍をぬいて大蛇をづた／＼に切り給ふ。其中に一の尾の至て切れず。尊恠しと思食し、堅樣に破て御覽ずれば一の靈劍あり。是を取て天照大神に奉り給ふ。「是は昔高間の原にてわがおとしたりし劍也。」とぞ宣ひける。大蛇の尾のなかに在ける時は村雲常に掩ければ天の村雲劍とぞ申ける。大神是をえて、天の御門の御寶とし給ふ。其後豐葦原中津國の主として天孫を下し奉り給ひし時、此劍をも御鏡に副てたてまつらせ給ひけり。第九代の帝開化天皇の御時までは一殿におはしましけるを、第十代の帝崇神天皇の御宇に及で、靈威に怖れて天照大神を大和國笠縫里磯垣の廣きに移し奉り給ひし時、此劍をも天照大神の社壇に籠め奉らせ給ひけり。その時劍を造りかへて御守とし給ふ。靈威本の劍に相劣らず。

annotation.translation: In ancient times, when the revered one descended to Hinokawa in Izumo Province, the land gods, Ashitsuchi and Tebitsuchi, were present. They had a beautiful daughter, who was named Inada-hime. The three of them, a father, mother, and child, lived in tears. The revered one asked, 'How is it?' and they replied, saying, 'I have eight daughters. All were devoured by a great snake. Now the last remaining girl is about to be swallowed. That great snake has eight heads and eight tails. Each head and tail crawls into eight peaks and eight valleys. Spiritual trees and strange herbs grow upon its back. It has existed for thousands of years, though no one knows exactly how long. Its eyes shine like the light of the sun and moon. Every year it devours people. When parents are eaten, their children mourn; when children are eaten, their parents mourn. The sound of weeping from the south to the north of the village never ceases.' The revered one felt sorrow and arranged for this girl to be given in marriage to a certain man. He had her placed in a royal palanquin, filled eight boats with sake, and created a figure of a beautiful woman, setting her atop a high hill. The reflection of her shadow appeared in the sake. The great snake, thinking it was a person, drank the shadow until it was drunk and lay down. The revered one then drew the ten-sword bundle he carried and sliced the great snake into pieces. One of the tails, however, could not be cut through. The revered one, thinking it strange, broke it open with force and examined it; inside was a spiritual sword. He took it and presented it to Amaterasu-Ōmikami, saying, 'This is the sword I once lost on the plain of Takama.' It is said that when the sword was in the tail of the great snake, the village was always covered by mist, and thus it came to be called the 'Heavenly Village Cloud Sword.' The Great Deity accepted it and made it a sacred treasure of the Heavenly Gate. Later, when the Heavenly Grandson was sent down to rule over the Ashihara-no-Nakatsukuni, this sword was also presented alongside the sacred mirror. Until the reign of the ninth emperor, Emperor Kuka, it remained in one hall. But during the reign of the tenth emperor, Emperor Suijin, fearing its spiritual power, the Great Deity moved Amaterasu-Ōmikami to a vast place at Kasanui in Yamato Province, and this sword was also enshrined at the altar of Amaterasu-Ōmikami's shrine. At that time, the sword was remade into a protective amulet. Its spiritual power was no less than that of the original sword.

text: 天の村雲劍は崇神天皇より景行天皇まで三代は天照大神の社壇に崇め置かれたりけるを、景行天皇の御宇四十年六月に東夷反逆の間、御子日本武尊、御心も剛に御力も人に勝れておはしければ、清撰に當てあづまへ下り給ひし時、天照大神へ詣て御暇申させ給ひけるに、御妹いつきの尊を以て謹而怠事なかれとて靈劍を尊にさづけ申給ふ。さて駿河國に下り給ひたりしかば、其處の賊徒等「この國には鹿多う候。狩して遊ばせ給へ。」とてたばかり出し奉り、野に火をはなて既に燒き殺し奉らんとしけるに、尊はき給へる靈劍を拔て草を薙ぎ給へば、はむけ一里が中は草皆薙れぬ。尊又火を出されたりければ、風たちまちに異賊の方へ吹掩ひ、凶徒悉く燒け死にぬ。其よりしてこそ天の村雲の劍をば草薙劍とも名付られけれ。尊、猶奧へせめ入て、三箇年が間處々の賊徒を討平らげ、國々の凶黨をせめしたがへて上らせ給ひけるが、道より御惱著せ給ひて、御歳三十と申七月に尾張國熱田の邊にて終に隱れさせ給ひぬ。その魂は白き鳥と成て、天に上けるこそ不思議なれ。生捕の夷共をば御子武彦尊を以て御門へたてまつらせ給ふ。草薙劍をば熱田の社に納めらる。あめの御門の御宇七年に新羅の沙門道行此劍を竊で吾國の寶とせんと思て、竊に舟に藏して行程に波風震動して忽に海底に沈まんとす。即靈劍のたゝりなりと知て、罪を謝して先途を遂ず。元の如く返し納め奉る。然るを天武天皇朱鳥元年に是を召て内裏に置かる。今の寶劍是也。御靈威いちはやうまします。陽成院狂病にをかされましまして靈劍を拔せ給ひければ、夜るのおとど閃々として電光にことならず。恐怖の餘に投棄させ給ひければ、自はたと鳴て鞘に差されにけり。上古にはかうこそ目出かりしか。縱ひ二位殿脇に差て海に沈み給ふともたやすううすべからずとて、勝れたる海士人共を召てかづきもとめられける上、靈佛靈社に貴き僧を籠め種々の神寶を捧げて祈り申されけれども、終に失せにけり。其時の有職の人々申合はれけるは「昔天照大神百王を守らんと御誓ひ有ける其誓未だ改らずして石清水の御流れ未だ盡せざるゆゑ、日輪の光未地に落させ給はず、末代澆季なりとも帝運の究まる程の事はあらじかし。」と申されければ、其中に、ある博士の勘へ申けるは「昔出雲國ひの河上にて素盞烏尊に切り殺され奉し大蛇、靈劍を惜む志深くして八の首八の尾を表事として人王八十代の後、八歳の帝と成て靈劍を取り返して海底に沈み給ふにこそ。」と申す。千尋の海の底、神龍の寶と成りしかば二度人間に返らざるも理とこそ覺えけれ。

annotation.translation: The Heavenly Murakumo Sword was revered and kept at the shrine of the Amaterasu Ōkami for three generations, from Emperor Sujin to Emperor Keikō. In the fortieth year of Emperor Keikō's reign, during the rebellion of the Eastern Barbarians, His Imperial Son, the Great Yamato Takeru, whose heart was strong and whose power surpassed that of ordinary people, descended to Kiyosuke to pay homage to the Eastern Barbarians. He went to the shrine of Amaterasu Ōkami and asked for permission to leave. There, the Amaterasu Ōkami entrusted him with the Spirit Sword, saying, 'Take care not to be negligent.' When he descended to Suruga Province, the local bandits said, 'This land is full of deer. Please hunt and enjoy yourself.' They prepared deer for him and set fire to the fields to burn them. The Great Yamato Takeru drew the Spirit Sword he had been given and cut through the grass. For a distance of one ri, all the grass was cut. Since the Great Yamato Takeru also set fire to the fields, the wind suddenly blew toward the rebels, and all the bandits were burned to death. From that time on, the Heavenly Murakumo Sword came to be called the Kusanagi Sword. The Great Yamato Takeru continued to advance into the interior, and over the course of three years, he subdued bandits in various places and defeated the evil factions of the provinces, returning them to the capital. However, he fell ill on his journey, and in the seventh month of the thirtieth year of his life, he finally passed away near Atsuta in Owari Province. His spirit became a white bird and ascended to the heavens; this is truly miraculous. He entrusted the captured barbarians to his son, the Great Prince Takehiko, to be presented at the imperial gate. The Kusanagi Sword was enshrined at the Atsuta Shrine. In the seventh year of the reign of Emperor Jimmu, a Silla monk named Dōgyō stole the sword, intending to make it a treasure of our country. He hid it in a boat, but during the journey, the waves and wind stirred violently, and the sword was about to sink to the bottom of the sea. Realizing that this was the curse of the Spirit Sword, he repented his sin and did not complete his journey. He returned the sword as it was and presented it. However, in the first year of the Shōtoku era of Emperor Tenmu, the sword was summoned and placed in the imperial palace. This is the current sacred sword. The divine power of the sword is exceedingly great. Emperor Jōmyō, afflicted with madness, drew the sword, and at night, a brilliant light shone like lightning. Overcome with terror, he cast it away, and it clattered to the ground before being returned to its scabbard. In ancient times, such things were considered auspicious. Even if the sword were to be carried by a nobleman to the sea and sunk, it would not be easily recovered. Therefore, they summoned skilled sailors to search for it, and they also secluded respected monks in sacred temples and shrines, offering various divine treasures and praying earnestly, but ultimately, the sword was lost. The officials of that time discussed the matter, saying, 'Long ago, Amaterasu Ōkami vowed to protect a hundred kings. That vow has not yet been broken, and the waters of the Ishizuchi Shrine have not yet run dry. Therefore, the light of the sun has not yet fallen to the earth, and even in the degenerate age of later generations, the imperial fortune will not come to an end.' Among them, a certain scholar remarked, 'Long ago, at Hinokawa in Izumo Province, the Great Yamato Takeru was killed by the Great Serpent, which deeply lamented the Spirit Sword. annotation.summary: The Heavenly Murakumo Sword was revered and kept at the shrine of the Amaterasu Ōkami for three generations, from Emperor Sujin to Emperor Keikō. In the fortieth year of Emperor Keikō's reign, during the rebellion of the Eastern Barbarians, His Imperial Son, the Great Yamato Takeru, whose heart was strong and whose power surpassed that of ordinary people, descended to Kiyosuke to pay homage to the Eastern Barbarians. He went to the shrine of Amaterasu Ōkami and asked for permission to leave. There, the Amaterasu Ōkami entrusted him with the Spirit Sword, saying, 'Take care not to be negligent.' When he descended to Suruga Province, the local bandits said, 'This land is full of deer. Please hunt and enjoy yourself.' They prepared deer for him and set fire to the fields to burn them. The Great Yamato Takeru drew the Spirit Sword he had been given and cut through the grass. For a distance of one ri, all the grass was cut. Since the Great Yamato Takeru also set fire to the fields, the wind suddenly blew toward the rebels, and all the bandits were burned to death. From that time on, the Heavenly Murakumo Sword came to be called the Kusanagi Sword. The Great Yamato Takeru continued to advance into the interior, and over the course of three years, he subdued bandits in various places and defeated the evil factions of the provinces, returning them to the capital. However, he fell ill on his journey, and in the seventh month of the thirtieth year of his life, he finally passed away near Atsuta in Owari Province. His spirit became a white bird and ascended to the heavens; this is truly miraculous. He entrusted the captured barbarians to his son, the Great Prince Takehiko, to be presented at the imperial gate. The Kusanagi Sword was enshrined at the Atsuta Shrine. In the seventh year of the reign of Emperor Jimmu, a Silla monk named Dōgyō stole the sword, intending to make it a treasure of our country. He hid it in a boat, but during the journey, the waves and wind stirred violently, and the sword was about to sink to the bottom of the sea. Realizing that this was the curse of the Spirit Sword, he repented his sin and did not complete his journey. He returned the sword as it was and presented it. However, in the first year of the Shōtoku era of Emperor Tenmu, the sword was summoned and placed in the imperial palace. This is the current sacred sword. The divine power of the sword is exceedingly great. Emperor Jōmyō, afflicted with madness, drew the sword, and at night, a brilliant light shone like lightning. Overcome with terror, he cast it away, and it clattered to the ground before being returned to its scabbard. In ancient times, such things were considered auspicious. Even if the sword were to be carried by a nobleman to the sea and sunk, it would not be easily recovered. Therefore, they summoned skilled sailors to search for it, and they also secluded respected monks in sacred temples and shrines, offering various divine treasures and praying earnestly, but ultimately, the sword was lost. The officials of that time discussed the matter, saying, 'Long ago, Amaterasu Ōkami vowed to protect a hundred kings. That vow has not yet been broken, and the waters of the Ishizuchi Shrine have not yet run dry. Therefore, the light of the sun has not yet fallen to the earth, and even in the degenerate age of later generations, the imperial fortune will not come to an end.' text: さる程に、二の宮歸り入らせ給ふとて法皇より御迎へに御車を參らせらる。御心ならず、平家に取られさせ給て、西海の波の上に漂はせ給ひ三年を過させ給ひしかば、御母儀も御乳母持明院の宰相も、御心苦しき事に思はれけるに、別の御事なく返り上らせ給ひたりしかば、差つどひて皆悦泣どもせられたる。

annotation.translation: In this manner, when the Second Prince returned, the Emperor had his carriage sent to welcome him. However, he was unwillingly taken by the Taira, set adrift upon the waves of the Western Sea, and made to pass three years there. Consequently, his mother and the wet nurse, the Saishō of the Myōjōin, had thought it a distressing matter; but since he had returned without any other incident, they were all overjoyed and shed tears of joy.

text: 同廿六日、平氏の生捕共京へ入る。皆小八葉の車にてぞ有ける。前後の簾を上げ、左右の物見を開く。大臣殿は淨衣を著給へり。右衞門督は、白き直垂にて、父の車の後にぞ乘られたる。平大納言時忠卿の車も、同くやり續く。子息讃岐中將時實も同車にて渡さるべかりしが現所勞とて渡れず。内藏頭信基は、疵を蒙たりしかば閑道より入にけり。大臣殿さしも花やかに清氣におはせし人のあらぬ樣に痩衰へ給へり。されども四方見廻して最思ひ沈める氣色もおはせず、右衞門督はうつぶして目も見上給はず、思ひ入たる氣色也。土肥次郎實平木蘭地の直垂に小具足計して隨兵三十餘騎車の先後に打圍で守護し奉る。見る人都の中にも限らず、凡遠國近國山々寺々よりも、老たるも若きも、來り集れり。鳥羽の南の門、作道、四塚迄、ひしと續いて、幾千萬と云ふ數を知らず。人は顧る事を得ず、車は輪を廻す事能はず。治承養和の飢饉、東國西國の軍に、人種ほろびうせたりといへども、猶殘りは多かりけりとぞ見えし。都を出て中一年、無下に間近き程なれば、めでたかりし事も忘れず。さしも恐をのゝきし人の今日の有樣、夢現とも分かねたり。心なき怪の賤男賤女に至るまで、涙を流し、袖を絞らぬは無りけり。増て馴れ近附ける人々のいかばかりの事をか思ひけん。年比恩を蒙り、父祖の時より祗候したりし輩の有繋身のすてがたさに、多くは源氏についたりしかども、昔の好み忽にわするべきにもあらねば、さこそ悲しう思ひけめ。されば袖を顏に押あてゝ、目を見上げぬ者も多かりけり。

annotation.translation: On the 26th of the same month, members of the Taira clan, taken alive, entered the capital. All were in small eight-petal carriages. They raised the curtains at the front and back and opened the side viewing windows. The Great Minister was wearing pure white robes. the Right Guard Chief was riding behind his father's carriage in a white hitatare. The carriage of the Grand Counselor Taira no Tokutada, also, continued in the same manner. His son, the Sanuki no Chujo Tokonari, should have crossed in the same carriage, but he was unable to do so, being detained at the current location. Kurado no Kamonori, who had received a wound, entered through a side path. The Great Minister, who had been so splendid and radiant in spirit, appeared emaciated and diminished. Yet, looking around in all directions, he showed no sign of deep sorrow. The Right Guard Chief, however, kept his head bowed and did not even raise his eyes; this was a sign of deep contemplation. Tofu no Jiro Saneyuki, dressed in a mokujiki hitatare with only light armor, led thirty-odd retainers who surrounded the carriages at the front and rear, offering protection. People from all over, not just from the capital, gathered from distant and nearby provinces, from mountains and temples alike; the old and the young all came together. From the southern gate of Toba to Sakado and Yotsuka, they continued in a dense stream, numbering in the tens of millions, a count beyond comprehension. People could not look back, and the carriages could not turn their wheels. Although it is said that during the famines of the Jisho and Gennan periods, or in the wars between the Eastern and Western provinces, the human race was nearly extinguished, it still seemed that many survivors remained. Having been away from the capital for a year, and with the time now drawing near, one could not forget such joyous events. The current state of a person who had once inspired such fear could not be distinguished from a dream or an illusion. Even the lowest of spirits, the base men and women, shed tears and wrung their sleeves; there was none who did not. One can only imagine how much the people, who had grown accustomed and close to him, must have felt. Having received his grace over many years, and having served since the time of their ancestors, many, though attached to the Minamoto clan out of reluctance to abandon their ties, could not so easily forget their past affections; thus, they must have felt such profound sorrow. Therefore, many pressed their sleeves to their faces and did not raise their eyes.

text: 大臣殿の御牛飼は、木曾が院參の時、車遣損じて切られにける次郎丸が弟、三郎丸也。西國にては、かり男に成たりしが、いま一度大臣殿の御車をつかまつらんと思ふ志ふかゝりければ、鳥羽にて判官に申けるは、「舎人牛飼など申者は、いふかひなき下臈の果にて候へば、心有るべきでは候はねども年來めしつかはれまゐらせて候御志淺からず。然るべう候はゞ御ゆるされを蒙て、大臣殿の最後の御車を仕り候はばや。」とあながちに申ければ、判官「仔細あるまじ、とう／＼。」とてゆるされけり。斜ならず悦で、尋常にしやうぞき、懷より遣繩取出しつけかへ、涙に暮て行先も見えねども、袖を顏に押あてゝ牛の行に任せつゝ、泣々遣てぞ罷りける。法皇は六條東洞院に御車を立て叡覽あり。公卿殿上人の車ども同じう立竝べたり。さしも御身近う召仕はれしかば、法皇もさすが御心弱う、哀にぞ思食されける。供奉の人人は只夢とのみこそ思はれけれ。「日比は如何にもして、あの人々に目をもかけられ、詞の末にも懸らばやとこそ思ひしかば、かゝるべしとは誰か思ひし。」とて、上下涙を流しけり。一年宗盛公内大臣に成て、悦び申し給ひし時は公卿には花山院大納言を始として、十二人扈從して遣り續け給へり。殿上人には藏人頭親宗以下十六人前驅す。公卿も殿上人も、今日を晴ときらめいてこそ有しか、中納言四人、三位中將も三人迄おはしき。軈て此平大納言もその時は左衞門督にておはしき。御前へ召され參せて御引出物給はて持成され給ひし有樣目出たかりし儀式ぞかし。今日は月卿雲客一人もしたがはず、同じく壇浦にて生捕にせられたりし侍共廿餘人白き直垂著て、馬の上にしめつけてぞ渡されける。六條を東へ河原までわたされて、歸て、大臣殿父子は九郎判官の宿所、六條堀河にぞおはしける。御物参らせたりしかども胸せき塞て、御箸をだにも立てられず。互に物は宣はねども目を見合せて隙なく涙をぞ流されける。夜になれども、裝束もくつろげ給はず、袖を片敷て臥給ひたりけるが、御子右衞門督に、御袖を打著せ給ふを、まぼり奉る源八兵衞、江田源三、熊井太郎是を見て、「哀高も賤きも恩愛の道程悲しかりける事はなし。御袖を著せ奉りたらばいく程の事か有るべきぞ。せめての御志の深さかな。」とて、武きものゝふども皆涙をぞ流しける。

annotation.translation: The minister's oxherd was Jiro-maru's younger brother, Saburo-maru, who was cut down during the time of the Imperial Visit to Kiso, when the carriage was damaged. In the western provinces, he had become a servant, but his heart was set on once again serving the minister's carriage, so at Toba he pleaded with the General: 'If one were to call oneself a retainer or oxherd, it would be the lot of a lowly and worthless servant; though there is no doubt that my heart is not lacking, I have served you faithfully for many years. If it is appropriate, I pray to be pardoned and serve the minister's final carriage.' He insisted, and the General said, 'There is no need for hesitation; do as you wish,' and granted permission. Overjoyed, he did not behave abnormally; he took out the reins from his bosom, adjusted them, and, though his tears blurred his vision so he could not see the way ahead, he pressed his sleeve to his face and followed the ox's path, weeping as he departed. The Emperor set his carriage at Rokujō Higashi-dōin and gazed upon the scene. The carriages of the high-ranking nobles and courtiers stood lined up. Since the Emperor had summoned them so close, his heart too was surely moved, and he was filled with sorrow. The attendants merely thought it was a dream. 'I had hoped that today, somehow, I might be seen by those people and perhaps spoken to, and thus thought such a thing would happen, yet who could have imagined this?' With tears streaming down, both the high and low wept. A year later, when Lord Morimori became the Minister of the Interior and was filled with joy, he was accompanied by twelve nobles, starting with the Great Counselor of the Flower Mountain Court, and sixteen retainers, including the Chief Chamberlain Chikamune, led the way. The nobles and courtiers were all present, shining as if on a clear day; four Middle Counselors and three Vice-Ministers of the Third Rank were there. Soon, this Great Counselor of the Taira, who was then the Director of the Left Guard, was summoned and presented his gifts, and the manner of this joyful ceremony was indeed magnificent. Today, not a single noble or scholar accompanied him; instead, over twenty samurai, who had also been captured alive at Dan-no-ura, wearing white straight robes, were tied on horseback and led across. They were taken east from Rokujō to the riverbank, and upon returning, the minister and his son were at the residence of the Ninth General at Rokujō Horikawa. Although offerings were presented, his chest was constricted, and he could not even lift his chopsticks. Though neither spoke of food, they looked at each other without breaking eye contact and shed tears without pause. Even as night fell, he did not relax his attire; he lay down with his sleeve spread out, but when his son, the Director of the Right Guard, was about to put his sleeve on him, the source of his tears, Gen-hyōe of the Gen family, Egida Genzō, and Kumai Tarō, seeing this, said, 'Whether high or low, there is no path of love and affection more sorrowful than this. If you were to put on your sleeve, what trouble could there be? How deep must your resolve be!' With these words, all the warriors shed tears.

text: 同二十八日鎌倉の前兵衞佐頼朝朝臣從二位し給ふ。越階とて二階をするこそ有がたき朝恩なるに是は既に三階なり。三位をこそし給ふべかりしかども、平家のし給ひたりしを忌うて也。其夜の子刻に内侍所太政官の廳より温明殿へ入らせ給ふ。主上行幸成て三箇夜臨時の御神樂あり。右近將監小家能方別勅を承はて家に傳れる弓立宮人といふ神樂の秘曲を仕て勸賞蒙りけるこそ目出たけれ。此歌は、祖父八條判官資忠と云し伶人の外は知れる者なし。餘り秘して子の親方には教へずして堀川天皇御在位の時傳へ參て死去したりしを、君親方に教へさせ給ひけり。道を失はじと思食す御志感涙抑へがたし。

annotation.translation: On the 28th of the same month, the former Hyogo-no-suke Yoritomo, a courtier of the Junior Second Rank, was bestowed the rank. Although ascending two ranks at once is a rare imperial favor, this time he was promoted three ranks. He should have been granted the rank of Third Rank, but this was done out of aversion to the fact that the Taira clan had previously bestowed that rank. That night, at the hour of the ox, he was allowed to enter the Onmyo-dono from the offices of the Daidaijin and the Inner Palace. After the Emperor made his imperial journey and settled in, a special divine music performance was held for three nights. The Right Inner Palace Attendant, Ko-ke, received a special imperial edict and performed the secret piece of divine music called the Yumitate-no-Miya, which had been passed down in his family. He was highly praised for this, which was most auspicious. As for this poem, no one knew it except my grandfather, the Hachijo-no-danjo Sada-tada, a performer. It was kept so secret that it was not taught to his son or his teacher, but was transmitted during the reign of Emperor Horikawa, and he died shortly after. The Emperor, who thought that the way of the art would not be lost, felt such deep emotion that he could not hold back his tears.

text: 抑内侍所と申は、昔、天照大神天の岩戸に閉籠らんとせさせ給ひし時、如何にもして我容をうつし置きて御子孫に見て奉らんとて御鏡を鑄給へり。是猶御心に合はずとて又鑄替させ給ひけり。先の御鏡は紀伊國日前國懸の社是也。後の御鏡は御子あまの忍ほみみの尊に授け參せさせ給ひて、殿を同うして住み給へ。」とぞ仰ける。さて天照大神天の岩戸に閉ぢ籠らせ給ひて天下暗やみと成たりしに、八百萬の神達神集に集て岩戸の口にて御神樂を奏し給ひければ、天照大神感に堪させ給はず、岩戸を細目に開き見給ふに、互に顏の白く見えけるより面白といふ詞は始まりけるとぞ承はる。其時こやねたぢからをといふ大力の神よてえいといひてあけ給ひしよりしてたてられずといへり。さて内侍所は第九代の御門開化天皇の御時までは一つ殿におはしましけるを、第十代の帝崇神天皇の御宇に及て靈威に怖れて別の殿へ移し奉らせ給ふ。近き比は温明殿におはします。遷都遷幸の後、百六十年を經て、村上天皇の御宇天徳四年九月廿三日の子刻に内裡なかのへに始めて燒亡ありき。火は左衞門の陣より出きたりければ内侍所のおはします温明殿も程近し。如法夜半の事なれば内侍も女官も參り合はせずして、かしこ所を出し奉るにも及ばず。小野宮殿急ぎ參らせ給て内侍所既に燒させ給ひぬ。世はいまはかうごさんなれとて御涙を流させ給ふほどに、内侍所は自炎の中を飛び出でさせ給ひ、南殿の櫻の梢に懸らせおはしまし光明赫奕として朝の日の山の端を出るに異ならず。其時小野宮殿世は末失せざりけりと思食すに悦の御涙せきあへさせ給はず。右の御膝をつき左の御袖を廣げてなく／＼申させ給ひけるは「昔天照大神百王を守らんと御誓有ける其御誓いまだ改らずんば神鏡實頼が袖に宿らせ給へ。」と申させ給ふ御詞の未をはらざる先に飛移らせ給ひけり。即御袖に裹で太政官の朝所へ渡し奉らせ給ふ。近頃は温明殿におはします。此世には請取奉らんと思ひ寄る人も誰かはあるべき。神鏡も又宿らせ給べからず。上代こそ猶目出かりけれ。

annotation.translation: Indeed, the Inner Chamber is so called because, in ancient times, when Amaterasu Omikami wished to shut herself away in the Heavenly Rock Cave, she had a mirror cast so that she could leave her reflection behind and allow her descendants to see her. However, this did not please her, so she had another mirror cast instead. The former mirror is now enshrined at the shrine of Kii-no-Kuni no Hiyori no Kuni no Kakenu no Miyashiro. The latter mirror was bestowed upon the august Ameno-Oshikomimi no Mikoto, and with him she resided in the same palace." Thus it was said. Then, when Amaterasu Omikami shut herself away in the Heavenly Rock Cave and the world below grew dark, the myriad of kami gathered together and played divine music at the entrance of the cave. Unable to bear it, Amaterasu Omikami cracked the door open a tiny bit and peered out; seeing their faces so pale, the term "omoshiroi" (meaning "interesting" or "amusing") is said to have originated then. At that time, a mighty deity named Koyanetachikara, who was called "Yo-te-i," opened the cave, and it is said that it could not be closed again. Now, the Inner Chamber remained in the same palace until the reign of the ninth emperor, Emperor Monka; however, during the reign of the tenth emperor, Emperor Sujin, fearing the divine power, it was transferred to a separate palace. In recent times, it has been located in the Onmyo-den. After the capital was moved, one hundred and sixty years later, on the 23rd day of the 9th month of the 4th year of the Tenroku era, during the reign of Emperor Uda, the palace was first burned down in the middle of the night. The fire started from the position of the Left Guard, and since the Onmyo-den, where the Inner Chamber was located, was quite near, the incident occurred in the middle of the night. Neither the ladies-in-waiting nor the female attendants could respond, and it was not even necessary for them to flee from the place. The Princess of Onomiya quickly arrived, and by then the Inner Chamber had already been consumed by fire. The world was in such a state that tears of sorrow flowed from the emperor's eyes. Then, the Inner Chamber leaped out of the flames itself and hung upon the tips of the cherry trees in the South Palace, shining brilliantly, not unlike the morning sun rising over the mountains. At that time, the Princess of Onomiya thought, "The world has not yet been lost," and could not hold back tears of joy. Pressing her right knee and spreading her left sleeve, she wept and said, "In ancient times, Amaterasu Omikami made a vow to protect the hundred kings. If this vow remains unbroken, let the divine mirror dwell in my sleeve." Before this vow was fully fulfilled, it was miraculously transferred. Immediately, it was wrapped in the sleeve and delivered to the Imperial Court in the Chosho. In recent times, it has been located in the Onmyo-den. Who could possibly think of taking it into this world? The divine mirror cannot dwell here either. Only in ancient times was it truly auspicious.".

text: 平大納言時忠卿父子も、九郎判官の宿所近うぞおはしける。世の中かくなりぬる上は、とてもかうてもとこそ思はるべきに、大納言猶命惜うや思はれけん、子息讃岐中將を招いて、「散すまじき文を一合判官に取られてあるぞとよ。是を鎌倉の源二位に見えなば、人も多く損じ我身も命生らるまじ、如何せんずる。」と宣へば、中將申されけるは、「判官は大かたも情ある者にて候なる上女房などの打たへ歎く事をば、如何なる大事をももてはなれぬと承り候。何か苦しう候べき。姫君達數多ましまし候へば、一人見せさせ給ひ、親うならせおはしまして後、仰らるべうや候らん。」大納言涙をはら／＼と流いて、「我世にありし時は、娘共をば女御后とこそ思ひしか。なみ／＼の人に見せんとはかけても思はざりしものを。」とて泣かれければ、中將、「今はその事努々思食寄せ給ふべからず。當腹の姫君の十八に成り給ふを。」と申されけれども、大納言それをば猶悲しき事に覺して、先の腹の姫君の十八に成り給ふを。」と申されけれども、大納言それをば猶悲しき事に覺して、先の腹の姫君の二十三になり給ふをぞ、判官には見られける。是も年こそすこし長しうおはしけれど眉目容美しう、心ざま優におはしければ、判官ありがたう思ひ奉て、もとの上河越太郎重頼が娘も有しかども、是をば別の方に尋常にしつらうてもてなしけり。さて女房件の文の事を宣ひ出されたりければ、判官剩へ封をも解かず、急ぎ時忠卿の許へ送られけり。大納言斜ならず悦で、やがて燒ぞ棄てられける。如何なる文共にてありけん、覺束なうぞ聞えし。

annotation.translation: The Taira no Dainagon Tokitada and his son were also near the lodging of the Kyūgorō no Kangō. Given that the world has become as it is, one should certainly think this way; yet the Dainagon, perhaps fearing the loss of his life, summoned his son, the Sanuki no Chūjō, saying, "A letter that should not have been scattered has been taken by the Kangō. If this is shown to the Gen no Ni-i in Kamakura, many people will be harmed, and my own life will not be spared. What shall I do?" The Chūjō replied, "The Kangō is a man of great compassion; it is reported that he cannot bear to see ladies-in-waiting struck or sighing over anything. He must be suffering greatly. Since there are many princesses, might it not be appropriate to show him one, to make him recognize her as a daughter, and then seek his permission?" The Dainagon wept, tears streaming down, saying, "When I was in the world, I had thought of my daughters as becoming Empresses or Queens. I never even imagined that they would be shown to common people." Though the Chūjō said, "Now you must not dwell on that matter so intensely. Your own princess has now reached the age of eighteen," the Dainagon still regarded this as a sorrowful thing, thinking of the princess from his previous marriage, who had reached the age of twenty-three, and how she had been seen by the Kangō. Though her age was somewhat advanced, her features were beautiful, her manner gentle, and the Kangō held her in high regard. Although there was also a daughter of the former Urawagoe no Taro Shigeyori, she was treated separately and with ordinary care. Then, when the lady-in-waiting mentioned the matter of the letter, the Kangō did not even open the seal but immediately sent it to Tokitada. The Dainagon was not displeased but delighted, and he promptly burned and discarded it. Whatever letter it may have been, we could not hear clearly.

text: 平家滅びて、いつしか國々靜まり、人のかよふも煩なし。都も穩しかりければ、「唯九郎判官程の人はなし。鎌倉の源二位は何事をか爲出したる。世は一向判官の儘にてあらばや。」などいふ事を源二位漏聞いて、「こは如何に、頼朝がよく計ひて、兵を指上すればこそ平家はたやすう滅びたれ。九郎ばかりしては、爭か世をばしづむべき。人のかくいふに奢て何しか世を我儘にしたるにこそ。人こそ多けれ、平大納言の聟になて、大納言を扱ふなるも受けられず。又世にもはゞからず、大納言の聟取いはれなし。是へ下ても定て過分の振舞せんずらん。」とぞ宣ひける。

annotation.translation: The Heike were destroyed, and before long the provinces grew quiet, and no one came to cause trouble. The capital also became peaceful, so they said, 'There is no one like the ninth son, the Judge; what has the Genji of the Second Rank in Kamakura done? If the world had remained entirely as the Judge wished, would it have been so?' When the Second Rank overheard them saying such things, he declared, 'How can this be? It was because Yoritomo planned so well and raised an army that the Heike were easily destroyed. With only the ninth son, how could he have quieted the world? Because people speak thus arrogantly, they have tried to make the world their own whim. Even if there are many, as the son-in-law of the Great Counselor Minamoto no Taira, even if he handles the Great Counselor, he cannot be accepted. Furthermore, in the world, there is no way to take the Great Counselor's son-in-law. Even in this situation, I will surely act beyond my station.' And so he proclaimed.

text: 同五月七日、九郎大夫判官平氏の生捕共相具して關東へ下向と聞えしかば、大臣殿判官の許へ使者を立てゝ、「明日關東へ下向と承候。恩愛の道は思切られぬ事にて候也。生捕の中に、八歳の童と附られて候ひしものは、未だ此世に候やらん。今一度見候ばや。」と宣ひ遣されたりければ、判官の返事には、「誰も恩愛の道は思切られぬ事にて候へば、誠にさこそ思食され候らめ。」とて、河越小太郎重房がもとに預り奉たりけるを大臣殿の許へわか君入れ奉るべき由、宣ひければ、人に車借て、乘せ奉り、女房二人著奉たりしも一つ車に乘り具して大臣殿へぞ參られける。若君は遙に父を見奉り給て、世に嬉氣におぼしたり。大臣殿、「如何に是へ。」と宣へば、やがて御膝の上に參り給ふ。大臣殿若君の御ぐしを掻撫で、涙をはら／＼と流いて、守護の武士共に宣ひけるは、「是は、各聞き給へ、母も無き者にてあるぞとよ。此子が母は、是を産とて、産をば平かにしたりしかども、やがてうちふして惱みしが、終に空く成ぞとよ。『此後如何なる人の腹に公達を設け給ふとも、思ひかへずして、生立て我形見に御覽ぜよ。さしはなて乳母などの許へ遣すな。』と云ひし事の不便さに、『あの右衞門督をば朝敵を平げん時は、大將軍をせさせ、是をば副將軍をせさせんずれば。』とて、名を副將と附たりしかば、斜ならず嬉氣に思ひて既に限りの時迄も、名を呼などして愛せしが、七日といふに、墓なく成りて有ぞとよ。此子を見る度ごとには、其事が忘れがたくおぼゆる也。」とて涙もせきあへ給はねば守護の武士共も、皆袖をぞ絞りける。右衞門督も[3]なき給へは乳母も袖を絞けり。やゝ久しく有て大臣殿、「さらば副將、とく歸れ。嬉しう見つる。」と宣へども、若君歸り給はず。右衞門督是を見て涙を押へて宣ひけるは、「やゝ副將御前、今夜は疾々歸れ。唯今客人のこうずるぞ。朝は急ぎ參れ。」と宣へども、父の御淨衣の袖にひしと取附て、「いなや歸じ。」とこそ泣給へ。かくて遙に程歴れば、日も漸暮れにけり。さてしもあるべき事ならねば、乳母の女房抱取て、御車に乘せ奉り、二人の女房共も袖を顏に推當てゝ、泣々暇申つゝ共に乘てぞ出にける。大臣殿は後を遙に御覽じ送て、日來の戀しさは事の數ならずとぞ悲み給ふ。「此子は母の遺言が無慚なれば。」とて乳母の許へも遣さず、朝夕御前にてそだて給ふ。三歳にて始冠して、義宗とぞ名乘せける。やう／＼生立給ふまゝに、みめ容美しく、心樣優におはしければ、大臣殿もかなしういとほしき事におぼして、西海の旅の空、浪の上、船の中の住にも片時も離れ給はず。然るを軍破れて後は、今日ぞ互に見給ひける。

annotation.translation: On the seventh day of that fifth month, when it was heard that the young lord of the Heike clan, the ninth son, the Dainagon, and others, were to be captured alive and go down to the Eastern Provinces, the Minister sent a messenger to the Dainagon's residence, saying, "I have heard that you will depart for the Eastern Provinces tomorrow. The path of love cannot be cut off. Among those captured alive, the eight-year-old boy who was with you, I wonder if he is still alive in this world. If I could see him once more." The messenger was dispatched. In response, the Dainagon said, "Since the path of love cannot be cut off by anyone, I am sure you must be thinking the same." Therefore, the boy was entrusted to Kawanishi no Saemon Shigenobu, and it was announced that he should be brought to the Minister's residence. People borrowed a carriage, placed him inside, and two female attendants dressed him, and together they entered the carriage and went to the Minister. The young lord, from afar, saw his father and was filled with joy in the world. The Minister said, "How is this?" and he immediately came and sat upon his father's knees. The Minister stroked the young lord's hair, tears streamed down his face, and he said to the guardian warriors, "Listen to each of you: this is a child without a mother. His mother, though she gave birth to him calmly, soon fell ill with sorrow and ultimately died in vain. She said, 'Whatever man you may bear a son to in the future, do not change your mind, but raise him as my keepsake and look upon him. Do not send him away to a wet nurse or others.' Because of the inconvenience of that matter, 'When we quell the morning enemy, let that Uemon no Daii become the Great General, and let this one become the Deputy General.' So they gave him the name Deputy General. He was not at all happy, and loved him, calling him by name until the appointed time. But now, on the seventh day, he has become a graveless being. Every time I see this child, I cannot forget that matter." Then, unable to hold back his tears, the guardian warriors also all squeezed their sleeves. Uemon no Daii, even if he had not wept, the wet nurse would have squeezed her sleeves. After a while, the Minister said, "Then, Deputy General, return quickly. I am very happy to see you." But the young lord did not return. Seeing this, Uemon no Daii held back his tears and said, "A little more, Deputy General, before your presence. Return quickly tonight. I am now hosting guests. Come early in the morning." But he clung tightly to his father's pure sleeve, crying, "No, I will not return." Thus, after a long journey, the day gradually set. Since there was nothing else to be done, the wet nurse took the child in her arms, placed him in the carriage, and the two female attendants, pressing their sleeves to their faces, saying farewell while weeping, together entered the carriage and departed. The Minister looked back from afar and sent them off; the longing of the past days was beyond number, and he mourned. "This child has no mother's will to be ashamed of," so he did not send him to the wet nurse, but raised him day and night before his own presence. At the age of three, he first underwent the coming-of-age ceremony, and was named Yoshimune. As he grew up in various ways, his appearance was beautiful, and his heart was gentle, so the Minister thought it was sad and pitiful, and did not leave even for a moment from the sky of the Western Sea journey, the waves, or the residence within the boat. However, after the army was defeated, today is the first time they have seen each other.

Come early in the morning." But he clung tightly to his father's pure sleeve, crying, "No, I will not return." Thus, after a long journey, the day gradually set. Since there was nothing else to be done, the wet nurse took the child in her arms, placed him in the carriage, and the two female attendants, pressing their sleeves to their faces, saying farewell while weeping, together entered the carriage and departed. The Minister looked back from afar and sent them off; the longing of the past days was beyond number, and he mourned. "This child has no mother's will to be ashamed of," so he did not send him to the wet nurse, but raised him day and night before his own presence. At the age of three, he first underwent the coming-of-age ceremony, and was named Yoshimune. As he grew up in various ways, his appearance was beautiful, and his heart was gentle, so the Minister thought it was sad and pitiful, and did not leave even for a moment from the sky of the Western Sea journey, the waves, or the residence within the boat. However, after the army was defeated, today is the first time they have seen each other.

text: 河越小太郎判官の御前に參ていひけるは「さて若君の御事をば何と御計ひ候やらん。」と申ければ、鎌倉まで具し奉るに及ばず。汝ともかうも是であひはからへ。」とぞ宣ひける。河越小太郎宿所に歸て、二人の女房共に申けるは、「大臣殿は鎌倉へ御下り候が、若君は京に御留あるべきにて候。重房も罷り下候間、緒方三郎惟義が手へ渡し奉るべきにて候。とう／＼召され候へ。」とて、御車寄せたりければ、若君何心もなう乘り給ひぬ。「又昨日の樣に父御前の御許へか。」とて悦ばれけるこそはかなけれ。六條を東へやて行く。此の女房共「あはやあやしき物哉。」と、肝魂を消して思ひける程に、少し引下て兵五六十騎が程河原へ打出たり。やがて車を遣とゞめて、敷皮しき、「下させ給へ。」と申ければ若君車よりおり給ひぬ。世にあやしげにおぼして、「我をばいづちへ具してゆかむとするぞ。」と問ひ給へば、二人の女房共、とかうの御返事にも及ばず。重房が郎等、太刀をひきそばめて、左の方より御後に立囘り、既に斬奉らんとしけるを、若君見つけ給ひて、幾程遁るべき事の樣に、急ぎ乳母の懷の中へぞ逃入給ふ。さすが心強う取出し奉るにも及ばねば、若君をかゝへ奉り人の聞くをも憚らず、天に仰ぎ地に伏してをめき叫みける心の中推量られて哀也。かくて時刻遙に推し移りければ河越小太郎重房涙をおさへて、「今はいかに思食され候とも叶はせ給ひ候まじ。とう／＼。」と申ければ其時乳母の懷の中より、引出し奉り、腰の刀にて押伏て終に頸をぞ掻いてける。猛き武士共もさすが岩木ならねば、皆涙を流しけり。頸をば「判官の見參にいれん。」とて取て行く。乳母の女房、徒跣にて追著て、「何かくるしう候べき。御頸ばかりをば給はて後世を弔ひまゐらせん。」と申せば、判官も世に哀氣に思ひ涙をはら／＼と流いて「誠にさこそは思ひ給らめ。最もさあるべし。とう／＼。」とてたびにけり。是を取て懷に入れて泣々京の方へ歸るとぞ見えし。其後五六日して、桂川に女房二人身をなげたる事ありけり。一人少なき人の頸をふところに入沈みたりけるは、此若君の乳母の女房にてぞ有ける。今一人屍を抱いて有けるは、介錯の女房なり。乳母が思きるは、せめて如何せん、介錯の女房さへ、身を投けるこそ有がたけれ。

annotation.translation: When they approached the presence of Kawanoe no Sataro no Kanjo and said, "How shall we now plan for our young lord?" he replied, "It is not necessary to go all the way to Kamakura. You two should also consider this." Thus he declared. Returning to his lodging, Kawanoe no Sataro, both female attendants said, "The Minister is descending to Kamakura, but the young lord should remain in Kyoto. Since Shigefusa is also descending, it would be proper to entrust him to Ogata Saburo Tadayoshi. Please be summoned at once." Since the carriage was brought forward, the young lord, without any particular thought, boarded it. "As if to his father's presence again as yesterday," they thought, how futile this joy was. They proceeded eastward toward Rokujō. These two female attendants thought, "How strange, how wonderful!" while their souls were consumed with worry. As they drew back a little, about fifty to sixty horsemen appeared at the riverbank. They immediately stopped the carriage, spread mats, and said, "Please dismount." The young lord descended from the carriage. Perceiving it as highly suspicious in the world, he asked, "You intend to take me to the river, do you?" The two female attendants could not even offer a proper reply. Shigefusa's retainers drew their swords, turned around from the left side to stand behind him, and were already about to strike him down. When the young lord realized this, as if he might be able to flee for a while, he hurriedly fled into the lap of his wet nurse. Since it was not even necessary to force her to take him out with great determination, he was held by the young lord, and without caring whether others heard, he looked up to the sky, bowed to the ground, and wailed and cried; his heart was pitiable to be imagined. Thus, as time passed slowly, Kawanoe no Sataro Shigefusa, holding back his tears, said, "Even if you now think of anything, it cannot be granted. Very well." Then, from the lap of the wet nurse, he was taken out, and with the sword at his waist, he was suppressed and finally cut off his neck. Even fierce warriors, since they were not like rocks, all shed tears. His neck was taken and carried, saying, "I shall present it to the Kanjo." The wet nurse, barefoot, pursued them, saying, "How painful it must be. Please grant only the neck, so that I may mourn for the next life." The Kanjo, thinking it extremely pitiful in the world, shed tears copiously, saying, "Indeed, you must have thought so. Most certainly so. Very well." Thus, taking it into his arms, weeping, he returned toward Kyoto. After five or six days, it happened that two female attendants threw themselves into the Katsura River. One, with the neck of a person of few years in her bosom, was the wet nurse of the young lord. The other, embracing a corpse, was the female attendant who performed the seppuku. The wet nurse thought, "At least, how can it be? Even the female attendant who performed the seppuku throwing herself is rare indeed."

text: さる程に大臣殿父子は九郎大夫判官に具せられて七日の曉關東へ下給ふ。粟田口を過ぎ給へば、大内山も雲井の餘所に隔りぬ。逢阪にもなりしかば關の清水を見給ひて、大臣殿なくなくかうぞ詠じ給ける。

annotation.translation: In this manner, the Minister and his son were accompanied by Kuwajiro Daibu no Gon, and on the seventh morning they descended to the Kanto. Having passed Awata-guchi, the Ōuchi-yama was also separated by clouds. Since they had reached Ōfusa, the Minister gazed upon the spring water of the pass and, with great reluctance, composed the following verse.

text: 道すがらも餘りに心細げにおはしければ、判官情ある人にて、樣々に慰め奉る。大臣殿、判官に向て「相構、今度親子の命を助けて給へ。」と宣ば、「遠き國、遙の島へも遷しぞ參せ候はんずらん。御命失ひ奉るまではよも候はじ。縱さ候とも、義經が勳功の賞に申かへて、御命計は助參せ候べし。御心安う思食され候へ。」と憑もしげに申されければ「たとひ夷が千島なりともかひなき命だにあらば。」と宣ひけるこそ口惜けれ。日數歴れば、同廿四日、鎌倉へ下り著き給ふ。

annotation.translation: Even on the way, because he acted so fearfully, the Danjo, being a man of feeling, comforted him in various ways. The Minister, turning to the Danjo, said, "Do not mind; this time, please save the lives of father and son." He replied, "Even if we are transferred to a distant land or a faraway island, surely we shall not survive until we lose our lives. Even if we do, after returning to the reward for Yoshitsune's meritorious deeds, your life may surely be saved. Please do not worry." Because he said this with such confidence, the Minister exclaimed, "Even if it be the thousand islands of the barbarians, if there is even a life worth living..." and was truly regretful. When the days passed, on the twenty-fourth day, they descended to Kamakura.

text:
梶原判官に一日先立て鎌倉殿に申けるは、「日本國は今は殘る所なう隨ひ奉り候。但し御弟九郎大夫判官殿こそ、終の御敵とは見えさせ給候へ。その故は『一谷を上の山より義經が落さずば、東西の木戸口破れ難し。生捕も死捕も義經にこそ見すべきに、
物の用にもあひ給はぬ蒲殿の方へ見參に入べき樣やある。本三位中將殿こなたへたば
ずば參て給はるべし。』とて既に軍出來候はんとし候しを、景時が土肥に心を合せて、
三位中將殿を土肥次郎に預けて後こそ靜まり給て候しか。」と語り申ければ、鎌倉殿
打頷いて、「今日九郎が鎌倉へ入なるに、各用意し給へ。」と仰られければ大名小名
馳集て、程なく數千騎に成にけり。

annotation.translation: Kajiwara no Hangan had already sent a message to the Kamakura-dono, saying, 'The land of Japan is now entirely in our hands. However, your younger brother, the Lord Kyūgō Daifu Hangan, appears to be our ultimate enemy. The reason is: "If Yoshitsune had not fallen from Mount Ichi-no-tani, the eastern and western gates could not have been breached. He should have been captured alive or dead, yet he has not shown himself for any purpose, and there seems to be no way for him to come paying his respects to the side of Lord Go-Sanmi no Shōshō. If Lord Go-Sanmi no Shōshō does not come here, he should come." Thus, they were already preparing to advance, but when Kagetoki aligned his thoughts with Tōi, and after entrusting Lord Go-Sanmi no Shōshō to Tōi no Jirō, things finally settled down.' When he had spoken thus, the Kamakura-dono nodded and said, 'Today, when Kyūgō enters Kamakura, each of you must make preparations.' Upon hearing this, the great and minor lords galloped together, and in no time, they numbered several thousand horsemen.

text: 金洗澤に關居ゑて、大臣殿父子請取奉て判官をば腰越へ追返さる。鎌倉殿は隨兵七重八重に居ゑ置いて我身は其中におはしながら「九郎はすゝどきをのこなれば此疊の下よりも這出んずる者也。但し頼朝はせらるまじ。」とぞ宣ひける。判官、思はれけるは「去年の正月木曾義仲を追討せしよりこのかた一谷壇浦に至るまで命を棄てゝ平家を責め落し、内侍所、璽の御箱事故なく返入奉り、大將軍父子生捕にして、具して是迄下りたらんには、縱如何なる不思議ありとも、一度はなどか對面なかるべき。凡は九國の惣追捕使にも成され、山陰山陽南海道、いづれにても預け、一方の固めともなされんずるとこそ思ひつるに、わづかに伊豫の國ばかりを知行すべき由仰せられて、あまさへ鎌倉へだにも入られぬこそ本意なけれ。さればこは何事ぞ。日本國を靜むる事、義仲義經が爲態にあらずや。譬へば同じ父が子で、先に生るるを兄とし、後に生るるを弟とする計なり。誰か天下を知らんに知らざるべき。剩今度見參をだにも遂げずして逐ひ上らるゝこそ遺恨の次第なれ。謝する所を知らず。」とつぶやかれけれども力なし。全く不忠なきよし度々起請文を以て申されけれども、景時が讒言によて鎌倉殿用ゐ給はねば、判官泣々一通の状を書て廣元の許へ遣す。其状に云く、

annotation.translation: At Kanarase, he was stationed, and the Minister and his son were requested to be taken away, and the Judge was ordered to be driven back at Koshigoe. The Lord of Kamakura had his seven and eight layers of attendants stationed around, while he himself was present among them, and said, "If Kyūgo is a man of good conduct, he will crawl out from beneath this mat. However, Yoritomo must not be provoked." The Judge thought to himself, "Since the first day of the lunar New Year last year, when we pursued and punished Kiso Yoshinaka, until this very day at Ichi no Tani and Dan no Ura, we have risked our lives to press the Taira clan, safely returned the Inner Palace and the Imperial Seal Box without incident, captured the Shogun and his son alive, and if we had descended to this point with such achievements, even if there were some strange matters, how could we not have met once? Indeed, I was made the Grand Pursuit Commissioner of all nine provinces, and was to be stationed in either the San'in or San'yō regions, or the Nankaidō, as a stronghold in one direction. Yet, I was only commanded to govern the small province of Iyo, and was not even allowed to enter Kamakura, which was my true intention. Therefore, what is this matter? To pacify the country of Japan is not the conduct of Yoshinaka or Yoshitsune. It is merely the plan to designate the elder-born son as the elder brother and the younger-born son as the younger brother. Who could claim to know the world if they do not know this? Moreover, to be driven away without even completing this audience is indeed a cause of lingering resentment. I do not know where to apologize." Although he murmured this, he had no strength. Despite repeatedly swearing oaths of loyalty, because the Lord of Kamakura did not employ him due to Kagetoki's slander, the Judge, in tears, wrote a single letter and sent it to Hiromoto. In that letter it says,

text: とぞ書かれたる。

annotation.translation: Thus it is written.

text: さる程に、鎌倉殿大臣殿に對面有り。おはしける所に庭を一つ隔てゝ、向なる屋に居奉り、簾の中より見出し、比氣藤四郎義員を使者で申されけるは「平家の人々に別の意趣思奉る事努努候はず。其故は池殿尼御前如何に申給とも故入道殿の御許され候はずば、頼朝爭か扶り候べき。流罪に宥められし事偏に入道殿の御恩也。されば廿餘年迄、さてこそ罷過候しかども朝敵となり給て追討すべき由院宣を給はる間、さのみ王地に孕まれて、詔命を背くべきにもあらねば、力不及、加樣に見參に入給ぬるこそ、本意に候へ。」と申されければ義員此由申さんとて、御前に參りたりければ、居なほり畏り給ひけるこそうたてけれ。國々の大名小名竝居たる其中に、京の者共幾らも有り、皆爪彈をして申しけるは「居なほり畏り給ひたらば御命の助り給べきか。西國で如何にも成給べき人の、生ながらとらはれて、是までくだり給こそ理なれ。」とぞ申ける。或は涙を流す人もあり。其中に或人の申けるは、「猛虎深山に在る時は百獸震ひ怖づ。檻穽の中に在るに及て尾を搖して食を求むとて、猛い虎の深い山に在る時は、百の獸恐怖ると云へ共檻の中に籠られぬる時は、尾を掉て人に向ふらんやうに、如何に猛き大將軍なれども、かやうに成て後は、心かはる事なれば、大臣殿も、かくおはするにこそ。」と申ける人も有りけるとかや。

annotation.translation: Thus it came to pass that there was an audience with the Kamakura-dono, the Minister. While he was seated, separated from the garden by one partition, he was residing in the opposite house; he looked out from behind the screen and said that Hikaru Fujiwara Yoshihira was sent as an envoy, stating, "The people of the Taira clan do not intend to hold any separate grudge. The reason is that, no matter what the Lady of Ike-no-dono may say, without the approval of the Late Cloistered Emperor, how could Yorimoto lend his support? The fact that they were pardoned and exiled is entirely due to the Late Cloistered Emperor's grace. Therefore, for over twenty years, they have indeed endured, but since an Imperial Decree was issued commanding that they be declared enemies of the throne and pursued for extermination, they could not, being so deeply embedded in the royal realm, turn their backs upon the Imperial Edict. Lacking the strength to resist, they have come to pay their respects in this manner, which is their true intention." Hearing this, Yoshihira, intending to report as such, went before the Minister. The Minister, however, remained seated and showed fear, which was most distressing. Among the great and minor lords of the provinces who were present, there were many from Kyoto; all of them plucked at their hair and said, "If you remain seated and show fear, will your life be spared? A man who could have done anything in the Western Provinces is now captured while still alive and has come this far, which is reasonable." Some even shed tears. Among them, one person said, "When a fierce tiger is in the deep mountains, it causes a hundred beasts to tremble in fear. But when it is caught in a cage or trap, if it wags its tail to seek food, even though one might say that the fierce tiger in the deep mountains causes the hundred beasts to fear, once it is confined in a cage, will it not wag its tail and face people? Thus, no matter how fierce a great general one may be, once one comes to this state, the heart changes; therefore, even the Minister, being in such a condition, is so." Such were the words spoken by some.

The fact that they were pardoned and exiled is entirely due to the Late Cloistered Emperor's grace. Therefore, for over twenty years, they have indeed endured, but since an Imperial Decree was issued commanding that they be declared enemies of the throne and pursued for extermination, they could not, being so deeply embedded in the royal realm, turn their backs upon the Imperial Edict. Lacking the strength to resist, they have come to pay their respects in this manner, which is their true intention." Hearing this, Yoshihira, intending to report as such, went before the Minister. The Minister, however, remained seated and showed fear, which was most distressing. Among the great and minor lords of the provinces who were present, there were many from Kyoto; all of them plucked at their hair and said, "If you remain seated and show fear, will your life be spared? A man who could have done anything in the Western Provinces is now captured while still alive and has come this far, which is reasonable." Some even shed tears. Among them, one person said, "When a fierce tiger is in the deep mountains, it causes a hundred beasts to tremble in fear. But when it is caught in a cage or trap, if it wags its tail to seek food, even though one might say that the fierce tiger in the deep mountains causes the hundred beasts to fear, once it is confined in a cage, will it not wag its tail and face people? Thus, no matter how fierce a great general one may be, once one comes to this state, the heart changes; therefore, even the Minister, being in such a condition, is so." Such were the words spoken by some.

text: 去程に九郎大夫判官樣々に陳じ申されけれども、景時が讒言に依て、鎌倉殿更に分明の御返事もなし。「急ぎのぼらるべし。」と仰られければ、同六月九日、大臣殿父子具し奉て、都へぞ返り上られける。大臣殿は今少しも日數の延を嬉き事に思はれける。道すがらも、「こゝにてや／＼」とおぼしけれども、國々宿々、打過々々通りぬ。尾張國内海と云ふ所あり。こゝは故左馬頭義朝[4]か誅せられし所なれば、これにてぞ一定と思はれけれども、それをも過しかば、大臣殿少し憑もしき心出來て、「さては命のいきんずるやらん。」と宣ひけるこそはかなけれ。右衞門督は、「なじかは命をいくべき、か樣に熱き比[5]なれは、頸の損せぬ樣にはからひて京近うなて切らんずるにこそ。」と思はれけれども、大臣殿のいたく心細氣におぼしたるが心苦しさにさは申されず。偏に念佛をのみぞ申給ふ。日數ふれば、都も近著て近江國篠原の宿に著給ひぬ。

annotation.translation: Although I had made my case to the various officials of the nine-robes on the outward journey, because of Kagehisa's slander, the Kamakura lord gave no clear reply at all. Since it was said, 'You must hurry and ascend,' on the ninth day of the same month, the Lord Minister and his son together set out and returned to the capital. The Lord Minister thought that a few more days would be a joyous thing. Even on the road, he thought, 'Perhaps here or there,' but passing through every province and every lodging, he went straight on. There is a place called Uchiumi in Owari Province. Since this was the place where the late Saemon no Kami Yoshitomo was executed, he thought that surely it would be here, but having passed it as well, the Lord Minister's mind became somewhat anxious, and he declared, 'Then surely my life will be spared,' which was indeed fleeting. The Uemon no Suke thought, 'How can I save my life? Since it is such a hot season, I must plan so that my neck is not injured and cut near the capital,' but because the Lord Minister felt so deeply distressed and anxious, he could not speak it. He only recited the Nembutsu. As the days passed, he arrived near the capital and reached the lodging of Shinohara in Omi Province.

text: 判官情深き人なれば、三日路より人を先立てゝ、善知識の爲に、大原の本性房湛豪といふ聖請じ下されたり。昨日までは親子一所におはしけるを今朝より引放て、別の所に居奉りければ、「さては今日を最後にてあるやらん。」といとゞ心細うぞ思はれける。大臣殿涙をはら／＼と流いて、「抑右衞門督はいづくに候やらん。縱ひ頸は落とも、體は一つ席に臥さんとこそ思ひつるに、生ながら別ぬる事こそ悲けれ。十七年が間一日片時も離るゝ事なし。西國にて海底に沈までうき名を流すもあれ故なり。」とて泣れければ、聖哀れに思ひけれども、我さへ心弱くては不叶と思ひて、涙を拭ひ、さらぬ體にもてないて申けるは「今はとかく思食すべからず。最後の御有樣を御覽ぜむにつけても互の御心の中悲かるべし。生を受させ給てよりこのかた、樂み榮え昔も類ひ少し。御門の外戚にて、丞相の位に至らせ給へり。今生の御榮華一事も殘る所なし。今又かゝる御目にあはせ給ふも、先世の宿業なり。世をも人をも恨み思食すべからず。大梵王宮の深禪定の樂み思へば程なし。況や電光朝露の下界の命に於てをや。たう利天の億千歳、唯夢の如し。三十九年を過させ給ひけむも、僅に一時の間なり。誰れか嘗たりし、不老不死の藥。誰か保たりし、東父西母が命。秦の始皇の奢を極めしも、遂には驪山の墓に埋もれ、漢の武帝の命を惜み給ひしも、空く杜陵の苔に朽にき。生ある者は必ず滅す、釋尊未だ栴檀の煙を免れ給はず。樂盡て悲來る、天人尚五衰の日に逢へりとこそ承はれ。されば佛は、『我心自空、罪福無主、觀心無心、法不住法』とて、善も惡も空なりと觀ずるが、正しく佛の御心に相叶事にて候也。如何なれば、彌陀如來は、五劫が間思惟して發しがたき願を發しましますに、如何なる我等なれば、億々萬劫が間、生死に輪廻して、寶の山に入て、手を空せん事、恨の中の恨み、愚なるが中の口惜い事に候はずや。努努餘年を思食すべからず。」とて、戒持せ奉り、念佛勸め申。大臣殿然るべき善知識哉と思食し、忽に妄念を飜へして西に向ひ手を合せ、高聲に念佛し給ふ處に、橘右馬允公長、太刀を引そばめて左の方より御後に立廻り、既に斬奉らんとしければ、大臣殿念佛を停めて、「右衞門督も既にか。」と宣ひけるこそ哀なれ。公長後へ囘るかと見えしかば、頸は前にぞ落にける。善知識の聖も、涙に咽び給ひけり。猛き武士も爭かあはれと思はざるべき。増て彼公長は、平家重代の家人新中納言の許に、朝夕祗候の侍也。さこそ世を諂ふならひといひながら、無下に情なかりける者かなとぞ、人皆慚愧しける。其後右衞門督をも、聖前の如くに戒持せ奉り、念佛勸め申。「大臣殿の最後如何おはしましつる。」と問はれけるこそ最愛けれ。「目出たうまし／＼候つる也、御心安う思召れ候へ。」と申されければ、涙を流し悦で、「今は思ふ事なし。さらばとう。」とぞ宣ひける。今度は堀彌太郎斬てけり。頸をば判官持せて都へ入る。屍をば公長が沙汰として、親子一つ穴にぞ埋ける。さしも罪ふかく離れがたく宣ひければ、加樣にしてんげり。

annotation.translation: Since the Kanpaku (Minamoto no Yoshitsune) was a man of deep affection, he sent a messenger ahead of him for three days' journey to invite the holy man named Tanzō of the Daimon Original Nature Temple to act as his spiritual guide. Until yesterday, father and son had been together in the same place, but from this morning they were separated and made to dwell in different locations. 'Surely, today must be our last day,' he thought, feeling deeply distressed. The Minister (Minamoto no Yoshitsune) wept copiously, saying, 'I wonder where the Right衛emon-no-dai is now. Even if my head should be severed, I had intended to lie down with my body in the same place. It is truly sorrowful to part while still alive. For seventeen years, I have never separated from him even for a day or a moment. The reason I have been known even to the depths of the Western Sea is because of this.' Then, the holy man, feeling compassion, thought to himself, 'If I too were to be weak of heart, I would not be able to fulfill my duty.' So he wiped his tears and spoke in a composed manner, saying, 'Now, you must not indulge in such thoughts. When it comes to viewing your final state, we should both mourn in our hearts. From the moment you received birth until now, your joy and glory have been unparalleled in history. You were a member of the Imperial family and attained the rank of Prime Minister. Now, nothing of your worldly glory remains. That you are now allowed to meet me is due to your karma from a previous life. Do not resent the world or people. If you contemplate the profound joy of the deep meditation in the Great Brahma Heaven, it will seem short. How much more so for the fleeting life of mortals, like lightning or morning dew? The ten thousand years of the Tāvatiṃsa Heaven are but like a dream. The thirty-nine years you have lived may seem long, but they are only a brief moment. Who has ever found the elixir of immortality? Who has ever preserved the lives of the Eastern Father and Western Mother? Even Qin Shi Huang, who pushed extravagance to its limit, was eventually buried in the tomb at Lishan; even Emperor Wu of Han, who cherished his life, rotted in vain in the moss of Duling. All living beings must perish; even Shakyamuni Buddha could not escape the incense of sandalwood. When joy ends, sorrow comes; even the gods and humans are said to experience the five signs of decay. Therefore, the Buddha said, 'My mind is inherently empty; there is no master of sin or merit; to observe the mind is to see no mind; the Dharma does not abide in any Dharma.' To regard both good and evil as empty is truly in accordance with the Buddha's mind. Why is this? The Amida Tathāgata, after contemplating for five kalpas, emitted vows that are difficult to conceive. How could it be that we, however humble, would, through countless kalpas, cycle through birth and death, enter a mountain of treasure, and leave our hands empty? Would that not be the deepest regret, the most foolish regret? Do not indulge in such thoughts for the remaining years.' With these words, he bestowed precepts and encouraged him to recite the Buddha's name. The Minister thought, 'What a worthy spiritual guide!' and suddenly turned his deluded thoughts, facing west, clasping his hands, and loudly reciting the Buddha's name. At that moment, Tachibana no no no Tōmō no Kimi-naga drew his sword and came around from the left behind him, intending to strike. The Minister, having stopped his recitation, said, 'Even the Right衛emon-no-dai is now gone,' which was truly sorrowful. Seeing that Kimi-naga was turning to strike from behind, his head fell forward. The holy man, the spiritual guide, also choked with tears. Even fierce warriors cannot help but feel compassion. Moreover, that Kimi-naga was a servant of the Taira clan, a trusted retainer of the Heike, serving the new Chancellor, attending to him morning and evening. 'Even so, one might say he was fawning upon the world,' yet he was not without emotion. All people felt ashamed. Afterward, the Right衛emon-no-dai also received the precepts from the holy man as before, and was encouraged to recite the Buddha's name. 'How did the Minister meet his end?' they asked, which was most beloved. 'He passed away with great joy; do not be distressed,' he replied. Weeping with joy, he said, 'Now I have no more thoughts. Farewell.' Then, Hori no Yatarō beheaded him. Yoshitsune carried the head and entered the capital. Kimi-naga took charge of the body, and father and son were buried in a single grave. Such a profound separation was declared, so they were added together in death.

text: 同廿三日大臣殿父子の頭都へ入る。檢非違使ども三條河原にいで向て、是を請取り、大路を渡して、獄門の左の樗の木にぞ懸たりける。三位以上の人の頸、大路を渡して獄門に懸けらるゝ事異國には其例もやあるらん。我朝に於は未だ其先蹤を聞かず。されば平治に信頼は惡人たりしかば、頸をばはねられたりしかども獄門には懸けられず。平家にとてぞ懸られける。西國より上ては、生て六條を東へ渡され、東國より歸ては、死んで三條を西へ渡され給ふ。生ての恥、死での恥、何れも劣らざりけり。

annotation.translation: On the same twenty-third day, the minister and his son entered the capital. The kebiishi came out to Sanjo Riverbank, seized them, crossed the main road, and hung them on the albizia tree to the left of the gibbet. For persons of the Third Rank or above, their heads are to be hung at the gibbet after crossing the main road; might there be such an example in foreign lands? In our country, we have yet to hear of any precedent. Therefore, since Taira no Noritsune was a wicked man during the Heiji Rebellion, his head was severed, but he was not hung at the gibbet; rather, he was hung at the gibbet for the Taira clan. Those coming up from the Western Provinces are brought alive to Rokujō and then sent east across the river, and those returning from the Eastern Provinces are sent dead to Sanjō and then sent west across the river. The shame of being alive and the shame of being dead were both no less than the other.

text: 本三位中將重衡卿は、狩野介宗茂に預られて、去年より伊豆國におはしけるを、南都の大衆頻に申ければ、「さらば渡せ。」とて、源三位入道頼政の孫、伊豆藏人大夫頼兼に仰せて、終に奈良へぞ遣しける。都へは入られずして、大津より山科通りに、醍醐路を經て行けば、日野は近かりけり。此重衡卿の北方と申は鳥飼中納言惟實の女、五條大納言國綱の養子、先帝の御乳母、大納言佐殿とぞ申ける。三位中將一谷で生捕にせられ給ひし後も、先帝に附まゐらせておはせしが、壇浦にて海にいらせ給ひしかば、武士の荒氣なきにとらはれて、舊里に歸り姉の大夫三位に同宿して、日野と云所におはしけり。中將の露の命、草葉の末にかゝて、消やらぬときゝ給へば、夢ならずして今一度見もし見えもする事もやと思れけれども、其も叶はねば、泣より外の慰めなくて明し暮し給ひけり。三位中將、守護の武士に宣ひけるは、「此程事に觸て情ふかう芳心おはしつるこそ、あり難う嬉しけれ。同くは最後に今一度芳恩蒙りたき事あり。我は一人の子なければ、此世に思ひおく事なし。年頃相具したりし女房の、日野と云ふ所に有りと聞く。今一度對面して、後生の事をも申置ばやと思ふ也。」とて片時のいとまをこはれけり。武士共さすが岩木ならねば、各涙を流しつゝ、「何かは苦う候べき。」とて許し奉る。中將斜ならず悦で、「大納言佐殿の御局は是に渡せ給候やらん。本三位中將殿の唯今奈良へ御通り候が、立ながら見參に入らばやと仰候。」と、人を入て言はせければ、北方聞もあへず、「いづらやいづら。」とて、走出て見給へば、藍摺の直垂に、折烏帽子著たる男の、痩黒みたるが、縁に依り居たるぞ、そなりける。北方御簾の際近くよて「如何に夢かや現か、是へ入せ給へ。」と宣ける御聲を聞き給ふに、いつしか、先立つ物は涙也。大納言佐殿は、目もくれ心も消果てしばしは物ものたまはず。三位中將、御簾打かついで、泣々宣ひけるは、「去年の春一谷で如何にも成べかりし身の、責ての罪の報いにや生ながら捕られて大路を渡され、京鎌倉に恥をさらすだに口惜きに、果は奈良の大衆の手に渡されて、斬るべしとて罷り候。如何にもして、今一度御姿を見奉らばやと思ひつるに、今は露ばかりも思置事なし。出家して形見に髮をもたてまつらばやと思へども、許されなければ力及ばず。」とて、額の髮を少し引きわけて口の及ぶ所をくひ切て、「是を形見に御覽ぜよ。」とてたてまつり給へば、北の方は日頃覺束なくおはしけるより今一入悲の色をぞ増し給ふ。「誠に別れ奉りし後は越前三位のうへの樣に、水の底にも沈むべかりしが、正しうこの世におはせぬ人とも聞ざりしかば、もし不思議にて今一度かはらぬ姿を見もし見えもやすると思ひてこそ、憂ながら今迄もながらへて在りつるに、今日を限りにておはせんずらん悲さよ。いまゝで延つるはもしやと思ふ憑みもありつる物を。」とて、昔今の事ども宣ひかはすにつけても、唯盡せぬ物は涙也。「餘りの御姿のしをれてさぶらふに、たてまつりかへよ。」とて袷の小袖に淨衣をそへて出されたりければ、三位中將是を著かへて、元著給へる物どもをば、「形見に御覽ぜよ。」とて置かれけり、北の方、「それもさる事にてさぶらへども、はかなき筆の跡こそ、永き世の形見にてさぶらへ。」とて、御硯を出されたりければ中將泣々一首の歌をぞ書かれける。

annotation.translation: The Third Rank Chunagon, Prince Tadanori, having been entrusted to Kano no Suke Mochishige, had resided in Izu Province since last year; when the great multitude of Nara repeatedly petitioned for him, saying, 'Very well, hand him over,' he was ordered by the grandson of Gen Sanmai Nyudo Yorimasa, Izu no Kurando no Daiyu Yorikane, and finally dispatched to Nara. He did not enter the capital, but traveling from Otsu via Yamashina-dori and through the Daigo road, he arrived at Hino, which was near. This Prince Tadanori's consort, known as the Northern Lady, was the daughter of the Naka-no-Kimi of the Takamori, the adopted son of the Gon-Dainagon Kunitsuna, the former Emperor's wet nurse, and was called Dainagon Sado. Even after the Chunagon had been captured alive at Ichinotani and received the Emperor's favor, he had remained attached to the former Emperor, but when he was cast into the sea at Dan-no-ura, he was captured by the rough samurai, returned to his old home, and lodged with his sister, the Daifu Sanmai, at a place called Hino. The Chunagon's life, like morning dew hanging on the tip of grass, was said to be extinguished, yet he did not wish to vanish; though he thought, 'Perhaps I might see her once more in this world, not merely in a dream,' since that could not be granted, he could find no comfort but weeping, day and night. The Chunagon spoke to the guarding samurai, saying, 'In these recent times, you have shown such kindness and noble hearts; I am most grateful and happy. I have one last request: to receive your favor one final time. I have no children, so I have no one left to care for in this world. I have heard that a lady who was once my companion, named Hino, resides in a place called Hino. I wish to meet her once more and discuss matters for the next life.' Thus, he was granted a brief audience. The samurai, though not as cold as rocks, each weeping, said, 'You must surely be in distress,' and granted his request. The Chunagon, though not entirely joyful, said, 'Please convey to the Dainagon Sado's residence that the former Third Rank Chunagon is now passing through to Nara; if he could pay a visit while standing, that would be most welcome.' He had a messenger enter and speak. The Northern Lady, hearing this, could not restrain her emotions and cried out, 'Where? Where?' and ran out to look; there, leaning against the railing, was a man wearing a blue-striped hitatare and a folded eboshi, thin and dark-complexioned, who appeared to be the one she sought. The Northern Lady, drawing near the curtain, said, 'Is this a dream or reality? Please let me in.' Hearing her voice, tears flowed before she could speak. The Dainagon Sado, with eyes averted and heart dissolved, remained speechless for a moment. The Third Rank Chunagon, pushing aside the curtain, weeping, spoke: 'Last spring, at Ichinotani, I should have perished; as retribution for my sins, I was captured alive and dragged along the public road, bringing shame to Kyoto and Kamakura. Finally, I was handed over to the great multitude of Nara, to be executed. I had wished to see your face once more, no matter what, but now I have nothing left to hope for, not even a drop of dew. If I were to become a monk and offer my hair as a memento, I would do so, but since I am not permitted, I cannot manage it.' Then, he parted his hair slightly at the forehead, bit it off where his mouth could reach, and offered it, saying, 'Please accept this as a memento.' The Northern Lady, who had been somewhat unsettled in spirit, grew even more sorrowful. 'Truly, since our parting, I should have sunk into the depths of water, like the Third Rank of Echizen, but I had not heard that anyone who was truly in this world would be lost; thinking perhaps by some miracle I might see your unchanged form once more, I endured this sorrow until today. But today marks the end of my life. The fact that I have been prolonged until now must have been due to some lingering hope.' As they exchanged stories of the past and present, the only thing that could not be expressed was tears. 'Your appearance is so frail; please return,' she said, offering a lined kosode lined with a plain garment. The Third Rank Chunagon changed into it and set aside his original garments, saying, 'Please accept these as a memento.' The Northern Lady replied, 'Even so, these are not mere trifles; may these traces of the brush become a lasting memento for the long world.' She then presented her writing box, and the Chunagon, weeping, composed a single poem.
